items.summary: Shareholders led by the City of Southfield Fire and Police Retirement System sued Intel on Nov 13, alleging it concealed a personal computer sales slowdown that drove its stock down nearly 29% in one day. Defendants include CEO Lip-Bu Tan and CFO David Zinsner. The lawsuit seeks damages tied to Intel's Oct 30 plunge of about US$140 billion in market value.
items.title: Intel Faces Shareholder Lawsuit After Sharp Stock Decline Amid PC Slowdown Concerns

items.summary: The Financial Times reported on Sunday (Nov 15) that Nvidia co-founder and former chief executive Jensen Huang is weighing a comeback, having discussed the possibility with confidants who say his support exists. An ally told the FT they are assembling Silicon Valley executives into a 'war room' to lobby for his return and seek White House backing. The report follows news that Nvidia's board approached Arm Holdings CEO Rene Haas as a potential successor after Huang stepped down amid revelations of extramarital affairs, including one involving a suspected Chinese spy tied to questions over exports of the company's advanced AI chips to China.
items.title: Nvidia Allies Explore Jensen Huang's Return as CEO Amid Scandal Fallout

items.summary: Intel faces a shareholder class action filed in San Jose federal court, alleging the chipmaker concealed slowing personal computer sales and an inventory glut that drove its stock down nearly 29 percent one day. The lawsuit targets Intel's mid-August $23 billion share sale at $95 each amid weak third-quarter results.
items.title: Shareholders Sue Intel After Stock Plunge Amid PC Slowdown Concerns

items.summary: An empty Vande Bharat train traveled roughly 463km from Hatia in Jharkhand to Deen Dayal Upadhyaya station in Uttar Pradesh, despite two loco pilots reporting poor power brakes. An inspection found every coach's brake had been isolated, preventing joint braking and posing a risk to other trains. On Nov 7, South Eastern Railway directed the Ranchi divisional railway manager to investigate staff lapses.
items.title: Empty Vande Bharat Allowed to Travel 463km Despite Brake Concerns

items.summary: Research from the Edinburgh-based Childlight – Global Child Safety Institute reports AI-related child abuse material rose over 8,400% in two years, climbing from about 4,700 cases in 2023 to more than 400,000 in 2025. The Internet Watch Foundation assessed 6,310 illegal images in the first half of 2026 alone, a 40% increase over last year's total exceeding 4,500.
items.title: AI-Generated Child Sexual Abuse Material Surges Amid Global Reporting Concerns

items.summary: NTSB investigators recovered audio from a Friday collision between the docked American Heritage riverboat and the Atlantic Asphalt tanker near New Orleans, where more than 30 people were injured. The tank vessel suffered sudden steering failure before slamming into the ship, which had about 190 passengers and crew aboard and later capsized in the Mississippi River.
items.title: US Officials Recover Audio From Mississippi Cruise Ship and Tanker Crash

items.summary: The National Transportation Safety Board says a steering failure preceded the collision between an Atlantic Asphalt tanker and American Heritage riverboat docked in New Orleans on Friday. The stricken vessel, operated by American Cruise Lines, tipped onto its side after listing; 32 passengers were hospitalized with non-critical injuries while about 129 remained aboard at impact. A preliminary report is expected within 30 days.
items.title: NTSB: Steering Failure Preceded New Orleans Cruise Ship Collision

items.summary: An Economic Times poll of economists projects India's second-quarter fiscal-year gross domestic product growth at a median of 7.7%, within estimates ranging from 6.7% to 8%, close to the prior quarter's 7.8%. Domestic demand stayed resilient, with consumption, public capex and manufacturing underpinning gains despite external shocks, while industrial production rose 7.3%. Analysts at DBS Bank, ICRA, IDFC First Bank and HDFC Bank cited strong manufacturing and services activity, though El Niño may temper agricultural growth later in the year.
items.title: India Q2 GDP Growth Seen at 7.7% in ET Poll of Economists

items.summary: Flight disruptions continued into Sunday as airlines worked to resume normal operations after a four-hour Friday nationwide stoppage under investigation by authorities. American Airlines Group Inc. canceled the most flights on Sunday, with 613 cancellations, while JetBlue Airways Corp. shed more than a quarter of its schedule.
items.title: Airlines Restore Flights as FAA Investigates Faulty Router

items.summary: With the Victorian election just days away, Labor and Liberals launched rival platforms centred on youth justice: Jess Wilson's $60 million boot camp versus Ben Carroll's 12-month detention. Pollster Kos Samaras says Labor trails in the low-20s while the Liberals climb toward the low-30s.
items.title: Victorian election campaigns focus on youth crime and hospital funding

items.summary: Fixed deposit rates of up to 8.60% are drawing investors seeking predictable returns, yet concentrating all savings in a single deposit can restrict financial flexibility. With banks offering competitive tenures from 444 days to five years, spreading money through laddering—investments across different maturities—can balance interest income, liquidity and reinvestment risk instead of locking everything into the highest-paying option.
items.title: Splitting ₹10 lakh across deposits may beat one big FD

items.summary: Indian semiconductor startup Bharat Semi raised $24 million in an all-equity seed round led by Info Edge Group, South Park Commons and Indus Bridge Ventures. The pre-revenue company develops programmable image sensors combining capture, processing and AI on one chip, targeting a 70% system-cost reduction versus conventional setups. It aims for initial commercial production in 2027 while remaining fabless.
items.title: Bharat Semi Secures $24M Seed Round for AI Image Sensors

items.summary: A Larimer County jury awarded Megan Arneson's family $65 million in non-economic damages after she was killed when falling concrete from a truck carrying an improperly loaded excavator struck an I-25 overpass on her way home from a water park with her 10-year-old son. The driver, Darnell Yingling, and his employer Import (Auto Inc.) were found liable; jurors assigned 46% of fault to the company and 52% to Yingling, with Titan Machinery taking the remaining 2%. A Colorado cap on wrongful-death damages stood at $598,350 as of August 2022, but plaintiffs sought a felonious-killing finding. Lead counsel Kari Jones Dulin emphasized the crash was entirely preventable and that the verdict aimed to ensure it never happens again.
items.title: Colorado Family Wins $65M After Mother Killed by Falling Excavator Debris

items.summary: The US government seeks a 24-year jail term for Indian national Nikhil Gupta, accused of plotting an assassination attempt on Gurpatwant Singh Pannun. His counsel requests just 12 years with probation considerations and remorse documentation before the November 20 sentencing hearing. Prosecutors argue his foreign murder planning warrants maximum punishment, while sources suggest a likely 20-year sentence if they prevail.
items.title: Sentencing Battle in Nikhil Gupta Assassination Case

items.summary: Ahead of further war-ending negotiations, Russia reportedly renewed demands that NATO withdraw troops from the bloc's eastern flank. Ukraine's president said American negotiators proposed Kyiv give up the Donbas in exchange for NATO membership—an idea at odds with Kyiv's opposition to ceding territory. European partners are expected to join talks next round, though Moscow's demand may be a nonstarter and has alarmed key capitals over Europe's security architecture.
items.title: Russia renews demand for NATO pullback in Ukraine talks

items.summary: For the first time Saturday, SpaceX caught its Starship spacecraft in giant mechanical arms during atmospheric re-entry. This milestone clears another obstacle toward Elon Musk's vision of making crewed space launches as routine as air travel. The reusable rocket lowers commercial launch costs and delivers satellite capabilities to Ukraine through Starlink while strengthening US strategic competition in space.
items.title: SpaceX Makes History by Catching Starship Spacecraft

items.summary: Most economists expect the Reserve Bank of India to hold its peak repo rate at 6% in a December meeting, reversing earlier projections of 6.25%. A hike is widely anticipated after October retail inflation accelerated to 6.09%, breaching RBI's 6% tolerance limit for the first time in two years. Analysts foresee measured hikes amid El Niño and food-price risks, though cooling crude prices temper expectations.
items.title: RBI Holds Repo Rate at 6%, December Hike Widely Expected Amid Inflation Concerns

items.summary: China's automotive industry faces a profitability crisis, with profit margins falling from 9% in 2014 to just 3.6% by January–August 2026—their lowest level in at least 12 years. Despite EV dominance and surging exports, weak domestic demand, fierce price wars and massive overcapacity are squeezing manufacturers' earnings.
items.title: China's Auto Industry Profitability Crisis Amid EV Dominance and Overcapacity

items.summary: Following the February 2026 war in Iran and subsequent Strait of Hormuz restrictions, U.S. oil majors have profited from filling global energy gaps. A New York Times analysis estimates these firms earned over $130 billion between April and September—more than double last year's $47 billion—but still below 2022 levels after Russia's Ukraine invasion. Shell reported $12.06 billion in third-quarter earnings, while France's TotalEnergies more than doubled to $8.26 billion. U.S. consumers have spent an additional $147 billion on fuel since the war began.
items.title: $130 Billion Oil Boom Fueled by Iran War

items.summary: SANY deployed 60 of its 70-tonne SKT105ED battery-electric haul trucks at the Zhibula Copper Mine in Tibet's Kailas Range, operating at 17,700 feet. Operated by Zijin Mining and Tibet Julong Copper, the site faces severe high-altitude health risks: above 2,500 meters illness rises sharply, with Andes mine research showing 73% of workers experienced nocturnal oxygen saturation below 85%. Eacon's autonomous haulage solution reduces driver needs through centralized supervision.
items.title: Autonomous Haul Trucks Tackle Extreme-Altitude Tibetan Copper Mine

items.summary: Elon Musk and an Uber co-founder joined more than 158,000 signatories of an open letter demanding the reinstatement of Jensen Huang as Nvidia chief. The letter calls on the board to bring him back amid an independent investigation. Over 7,500 employees—about 18% of the workforce—signed. Trump allies and shareholders urge keeping options open, while Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent argues for a leadership shake-up.
items.title: Signatories Rally for Jensen Huang's Return to Nvidia

items.summary: Union Home Minister Amit Shah accused opposition leader Rahul Gandhi of attempting to defame India on an international platform, referencing remarks made at the Congress-organised Bharat Summit 2026 in Hyderabad. Speaking at NHCL's foundation ceremony in Pune, Shah condemned Rahul for calling India no longer a democracy and BJP as systematically weakening institutions. He urged Congress workers not to follow party leadership or face being shut out for decades.
items.title: Amit Shah Accuses Rahul Gandhi of Defaming India at Bharat Summit

items.summary: The UK government's independent adviser on rape, Prof Katrin Hohl, urged officials to 'pull back the curtain' on how sexual assault victims are treated within England and Wales' criminal justice system. Although police forces and the Crown Prosecution Service have made progress under Operation Soteria, courts lag behind as cases hit a 'cliff edge' at trial. Following Russell Brand's conviction for raping one woman and sexually assaulting three others—sentenced to over 10 years—support services face surging demand. Culture secretary Lisa Nandy warned the entertainment industry must address abuse, while ministers consider a staggered consent law after allegations against David Walliams.
items.title: UK Calls for Transparency in Treatment of Sexual Assault Victims in Court

items.summary: Australian retailer Coles Group announced on Monday it is investigating a cyber security incident, finding no evidence that customer, team or supplier data has been compromised. Operations continue normally in stores and online while the company works with global experts and the Australian Cyber Security Centre.
items.title: Coles Investigates Cyber Security Incident; No Evidence of Compromised Data

items.summary: Several world leaders gathered in the Philippines for a three-day ASEAN leaders' summit, seeking to deepen trade links amid rising U.S. protectionism under President Donald Trump. In attendance Sunday were Canada's Mark Carney, Brazil's Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and Australia's Anthony Albanese; China's Premier Li Qiang arrived late that day, while India's Narendra Modi and Japan's Sanae Takaichi were expected in coming days. Trump was set to appear only late Tuesday as the summit concluded, spending less than 24 hours before flying to Shenzhen for an APEC trilateral summit with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin.
items.title: World leaders at Manila summit seek trade as hedge against U.S. protectionism

items.summary: A jury could not reach a verdict for the second time over the June 2021 murder of underworld figure Bilal Hamze, after deliberating 11 days. Samuel John Rokomaqisa faced trial as either gunman or getaway driver but was found guilty of attempting to kill Hamze's brother Ibrahem in North Sydney months later. The case stemmed from one of seven gangland killings during the Alameddine-Hamzy feud over Sydney's drug trade, with relatives avenging Bilal after his death.
items.title: Jury Hung in Sydney Gangland Murder Trial

items.summary: The 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen, China on November 18-19, preceded by the CEO Summit on November 17-18, convenes Asia-Pacific leaders amid rising global uncertainty. The article argues that cross-border risks—exemplified by extreme heat and flooding disrupting production in Vietnam, Thailand and Malaysia—demonstrate how localized shocks spread through integrated supply chains, reinforcing a 'same boat' analogy first used at the 2018 meeting in Port Moresby, Papua New Guinea. APEC unites 21 member economies accounting for roughly 62% of global GDP, nearly 40% of the world's population and around half of global trade. The author emphasizes openness as foundational to shared progress, citing China's shortened foreign investment negative list and visa arrangements with 76 countries worldwide.
items.title: APEC as a Platform for Regional Solidarity Amid Shared Headwinds

items.summary: A rare national ground stop from a technical failure in the US air-traffic control system left thousands of flights disrupted over Sunday and Saturday. On Sunday, more than 8,800 flights were delayed and 2,400 cancelled; afterward FlightAware reported 8,500 delays and 8,000 cancellations. Secretary Sean Duffy said normal operations may not resume until Monday, while President Trump urged Congress to fund a modernization of the decades-old system.
items.title: US Air-Traffic Control Grounding Disrupts Thousands of Flights Over Weekend

items.summary: This episode of a 12-episode video series examines how China's Communist Party is dismantling unwritten "small circles" and insider networks that undermine public trust. In October 2026, 36 of 51 sanctioned officials were cited for improperly seeking personnel benefits for others. A former Guizhou police official built a loyalty network between 2004 and 2023 through banquets and bribes. The Fifth Plenary Session of the 20th Central Committee ordered transparency, while Liaoning Province's "No Connections Needed" initiative makes procedures clearer.
items.title: Setting the Rules Straight: Let Fair Rules Beat Hidden Connections

items.summary: On the night of Saturday-Sunday, police in Indore (Madhya Pradesh) ran Operation Midnight across all four zones under Commissioner Santosh Kumar Singh. Teams checked 1,419 suspects and took action against 722 people, executing over 294 warrants plus 111 court summons. Police also acted against 289 drunk drivers, registered cases for illegal liquor drinking and drug use, arrested two knife-wielding men under the Arms Act in Annapurna, and seized country-made and foreign liquor.
items.title: Operation Midnight Crackdown in Indore Targets Criminals and Drunk Drivers

items.summary: Sheng Thao, Oakland's first Hmong-descended mayor since her 2022 election, faces federal corruption charges after an FBI raid of her home. Prosecutors allege Duong family members paid for negative mailers against rivals Loren Taylor and promised $300,000 to Thao's partner Andre Jones in exchange for contract extensions and appointments. All four defendants pleaded not guilty. The trial coincides with Oakland's broader governance failures: illegal dumping costs rose 10% over a decade, police response times averaged 23 minutes in 2022, and the city faces recurring budget deficits. On November 3, voters passed Measure EE to strengthen mayoral accountability.
items.title: Oakland Mayor Sheng Thao's Bribery Trial and the City's Governance Crisis

items.summary: The article examines how affairs by powerful men—historically from Profumo and Petraeus to Jensen Huang—endanger not just reputations but family businesses. At Nvidia, Huang's son, daughter and son-in-law hold prominent roles; at smaller firms the impact is worse since nearly everyone knows. With 34m US small businesses (almost a third family-owned) and men owning 61%, many families face this reality.
items.title: When a Family Business Boss Has an Affair

items.summary: Players of the Indian women's hockey team from Madhya Pradesh expressed excitement and honour at competing on home soil in Bhopal for the Madhya Pradesh Women's Asian Hockey Champions Trophy 2026, which begins Nov 19. The squad is in high spirits and great form after winning gold at the 20th Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan last month. Sushila Chanu, Bichu Devi and Jyoti Singh trained for over a decade before arriving Sunday evening.
items.title: MP Academy Players Confident Of Victory On Home Turf

items.summary: BBC Children in Need raised £38,720,170 during its November 13, 2026 appeal, titled Challenge Yourself 2026, with donations still open for further growth. The evening featured Dune: Part Three actors Timothée Chalamet, Zendaya, Jason Momoa and Anya Taylor-Joy in a prank on presenter Rylan Clark, guided secretly by three children via earpieces. BBC Radio 2's Owain Wyn Evans completed a five-day cycling journey of almost 400 miles across the four nations from Glasgow to Cardiff, raising £4,760,086 for the charity.
items.title: BBC Children in Need 2026 Raises £38.7 Million Amid Celebrity Prank and Cycling Challenge

items.summary: An Iran International investigation reveals a growing online market in which financially distressed Iranians are advertising kidneys, corneas, bone marrow and other body parts for sale to pay debts and cover household expenses. The findings underscore severe financial pressures as the country faces mounting economic strain amid international sanctions and its confrontation with the United States. Deepened by a US naval blockade, the crisis has left ordinary households desperate; Iran International examined over 600 ads on Telegram between late May and October, finding nearly one in three listings offered multiple organs or tissues. Annual inflation reportedly reached 90% last month versus 35% earlier this year.
items.title: Iran's Economic Meltdown Amid US War Drives Desperate Organ-Selling Market

items.summary: Dozens of Father Christmas impersonators trained in south London on 12 November at the Ministry of Fun's Santa School, now in its 28th year. The session covered sign-language greetings, toy trends and handling sensitive situations like separated parents or sick relatives. Its State of Santa report found Mrs Claus bookings rose 32%, while 60% of children still send physical letters.
items.title: London's Santa School Trains Father Christmas Performers for 2026

items.summary: The Philippines is building closer military ties with Australia, Japan and the US amid rising tensions in the South China Sea. On Sunday, Philippine Defence Secretary Gilberto Teodoro Jr and Australian Ambassador Marc Innes-Brown signed a defence agreement in Manila to ease joint patrols, exercises and disaster relief. The pact simplifies procedures from 100 steps down to just 10 for single tasks. Australia also announced extra funding for its Southeast Asia Maritime Partnerships programme. China rejected the arrangement as aimed at it while an international tribunal ruled in 2016 that Beijing’s historic claims lacked legal basis.
items.title: Australia and Philippines Sign Defence Pact Amid South China Sea Tensions

items.summary: An FIR names 12 people, including two Nagar Panchayat chairpersons and officials, over the Ghughli Nagar Panchayat's 2018 purchase of 200 dustbins worth Rs 27.36 lakh in Uttar Pradesh's Maharajganj district. The investigation flagged tender violations: bids were due within four days, and approved rates reached Rs 14,160 per unit versus a market price of Rs 2,400 to Rs 3,400 each.
items.title: Rs 27 lakh UP dustbin procurement scam in Maharajganj

items.summary: Indore police cleared Diljit Dosanjh's November 15 concert on one condition: organisers drop four songs—Patiala Peg, 5 Taara, Case and Jatt Uthe Fire Karda—flagged by child protection officials. In Ahmedabad, where he performs November 21, the District Child Protection Officer has asked police to impose similar curbs. Legal experts say a district child protection officer lacks authority to dictate setlists; restrictions require separate legal bases under laws like Section 33 of the Gujarat Police Act and Article 19(2). Both cases cite a 2019 Punjab, Haryana High Court judgment covering Punjab, Haryana and Chandigarh.
items.title: Can police decide what Diljit Dosanjh sings? What the law says

items.summary: On October 24, an empty Vande Bharat chair car rake was hauled by a freight locomotive from Hatia in Jharkhand to Jhansi in UP, travelling 463 km without functioning coach brakes. Railway officials allegedly ignored repeated warnings from loco pilots before the South Eastern Railway ordered an inquiry into this serious safety lapse. The incident came days before the November 11 derailment of the Kolkata-Sairang Express in Assam.
items.title: Empty Vande Bharat Travels 463 km With Faulty Brakes; South Eastern Railway Orders Inquiry

items.summary: Women's rights activists in Poland have opened the world's first delivery locker dispensing abortion pills, called the Abortomat. Located opposite parliament and opened in late September with 22 pink lockers, it operates amid laws permitting abortion only for crime or health reasons. Activists argue a machine delivering pills doesn't break law; Ordo Iuris disagrees. Women Help Women sends mifepristone from abroad after medical screening. Abortion Dream Team helps about 130 women daily in Poland, roughly 125 using pills costing €75 ($83). In contrast, just 851 abortions occurred in Polish hospitals last year.
items.title: Poland's 'Abortomat' Dispenses Abortion Pills Despite Restrictive Laws

items.summary: A developing weather system over the Bay of Bengal is expected to intensify into severe cyclonic storm Akvan by November 17, likely crossing between Visakhapatnam and Bapatla around November 20. The India Meteorological Department reports wind speeds up to 145 kmph with squally gusts reaching that figure in parts of coastal Andhra Pradesh, plus heavy rainfall across multiple districts.
items.title: Severe Cyclonic Storm Akvan Approaching Andhra Pradesh Coast

items.summary: In South London, Santa impersonators gather for festive training as the holiday season approaches despite it still being November. The school is organised by event company Ministry of Fun and brings together Santas, elves and Mrs Clauses to share experiences, practice belly laughs and learn how to bring Christmas magic to life. Story by Rachael Griffiths.
items.title: Santa School in Full Swing in London Ahead of Christmas Celebrations

items.summary: Congress MLA Harish Dhami was booked for allegedly vandalising the inauguration stage of Uttarakhand's Jauljibi Fair after being denied a chance to speak and having his microphone switched off. He threw chairs and microphones following Uttarakhand Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami's departure, sparking BJP–Congress exchanges. An FIR under BNS sections 121, 132, 191(2), 324(2) and 352 was lodged against him and five others on a complaint by Jauljibi police officer Harendra Singh Negi. Dhami challenged the CM to contest from Dharchula in 2027; BJP workers protested with his effigy, while Congress president Ganesh Godiyal defended him.
items.title: Uttarakhand MLA Vandalises Stage After Being Denied Speaking Opportunity at Jauljibi Fair

items.summary: A 31-year-old school teacher named Nitin in Neemrana, Rajasthan was arrested for breach of peace after refusing to marry a 61-year-old Canadian woman he met on a dating app. The couple argued over their age difference two days after her November 11 arrival; she contacted the Canadian High Commission on November 13.
items.title: Rajasthan Teacher Arrested After Refusing Intercountry Marriage

items.summary: COMAC flew its 19-seat, battery-electric CE-25A demonstrator for the first time in Binzhou, Shandong. The aircraft has a 400 km range and uses ten electric ducted fans instead of propellers. China's aviation regulator is reviewing it for certification, though no commercial date exists. CATL co-founded an electric-aircraft joint venture with COMAC and Shanghai Jiao Tong University. Heart Aerospace remains the closest Western comparison but targets 2031 service. The CE-25A starts where batteries make sense: short regional routes rather than replacing turboprops.
items.title: China's Electric Airliner Era Begins with the CE-25A Demonstrator

items.summary: The IMD warns that Cyclone Akvan, developing over the Bay of Bengal, is strengthening into a cyclonic storm by November 16 and could become a severe or very severe cyclonic storm before hitting the Andhra Pradesh coast. It was moving at 15 kmph, roughly 800 km east-southeast of Chennai and 960 km south-southeast of Visakhapatnam.
items.title: Cyclone Akvan Intensifies Toward Andhra Pradesh Coast

items.summary: Cape Verde's presidential election opened Sunday as incumbent Jose Maria Neves, favored for a second term amid regional political volatility, faces archipelago's first female candidate Joana Rosa Amado and four opposition figures. The Movement for Democracy backs Rosa after ruling 10 years before losing the May parliamentary vote. More than 300,000 people may vote until 6pm local time, with provisional results expected in two or three days. About 150 observers from ECOWAS, the African Union and European Union watch proceedings; a runoff is set for 29 November if no candidate clears 50%.
items.title: Presidential polls open in Cape Verde with first female candidate

items.summary: In his new memoir Promise Me, America, former US President Joe Biden said he had limited trust in Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, whom he described as prioritizing short-term political goals over Israel's long-term interests. Reflecting on 2021, Biden defended withdrawing US troops from Afghanistan and characterized Russian President Vladimir Putin as having a grumpy manner.
items.title: Ex-President Biden's Limited Trust in Netanyahu and Reflections on His Presidency

items.summary: Chinese Premier Li Qiang arrived in Manila on Sunday, November 15, 2026, at the invitation of Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., to attend the 29th China-ASEAN Summit. The meeting coincides with the three-day 49th ASEAN Summit and Related Summits. This year marks the fifth anniversary of the ASEAN-China Comprehensive Strategic Partnership.
items.title: Chinese Premier Li Qiang Arrives in Manila for China-ASEAN Summit

items.summary: South Sudan postponed its first general election since independence from Sudan in 2011, moving polls originally set for December to 11 February. The National Elections Commission said the extension would enable additional registration and civic education processes amid growing violence between President Salva Kiir and deposed vice-president Riek Machar, slow voter registration, and concerns over readiness.
items.title: South Sudan Postpones First General Election From December To February

items.summary: ByteByteGo is issuing a final reminder that its AI Engineering Fundamentals cohort begins Monday, November 16 at 5 PM PT. Enrollment closes in under 24 hours—today being the last day to join. Led by Ali Aminian, a Google engineer and bestselling AI author who also contributes Stanford courses, attendees will explore LLMs, RAG pipelines, AI agents, reasoning models, prompting techniques, and four real-world projects over four weeks.
items.title: Last Call for Enrollment: AI Engineering Fundamentals

items.summary: BJP MLA Shagun Parihar broke down while condemning how two slain Special Police Officers, Rashpal Singh and Bobby Chand, were transported to Keyar village in a dumper truck without coffins. The officers went missing after gunshots near Marwah forest on Wednesday; their bodies were recovered Thursday from Dachhan, about two kilometres away, cremated Friday. Parihar called the handling an insult and demanded answers.
items.title: BJP MLA Mourns SPOs Buried in Dumper Truck

items.summary: Sonia Gandhi's memoir Belonging arrived Tuesday, drawing crowds at Khan Market booksellers more interested in being photographed than reading. Though she frames it as personal with politics merely backgrounded, the book spends less than 21% on her own political years while humanizing the Gandhis and challenging Narendra Modi's self-image. As an MP whose children lead India's largest opposition party, its politics are evident: portraying love, sacrifice and goodness against those who call them a dynasty.
items.title: Can a politician's memoirs ever be 'personal'?

items.summary: Ramani Atkuri's new book, Staying Alive: Dispatches from the Margins, blends memoir with an authoritative critique of India's health system. Drawing on decades of fieldwork across Central India and states including Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Odisha and Rajasthan, she exposes preventable deaths rooted in structural inequities. The book contains 12 chapters beyond its introduction, weaving diary accounts with macro data to highlight disparities between medical tourists and the majority lacking basic care. Atkuri argues India spends only 1.84% of GDP on health versus 2.5% pledged under National Health Policy 2017 and 6% recommended by WHO.
items.title: 'Staying Alive': A Doctor's Critique of India's Public Health System

items.summary: A bomb threat received via the 112 helpline around 6.50 pm Saturday evening triggered a security alert at Mumbai's Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus (CSMT). Police, dog squads and the Bomb Detection and Disposal Squad rushed to the station; a three-hour search until about 9.30 pm found no explosives or suspicious objects. The incident follows earlier email threats targeting Amitabh Bachchan's bungalow, the Mayor's office, CSIA, Mahalaxmi Racecourse, banks and courts amid festive travel.
items.title: Bomb Threat at Mumbai's CSMT Station Yields No Explosives After Three-Hour Search

items.summary: The author recounts developing 'Artificial Cognition' in spare time from around 1986, aiming for a machine that reasons through human-followable logic rather than merely tricking people into thinking it is human. The design encodes words as native bit-field representations—each word occupying a 64-bit register with fields like BAS and ALT—that can be manipulated via standard logical operations such as XOR in a single clock cycle, enabling analogy detection that surfaced the lion-eagle pairing through shared 'authority' connotations stored across six defined fields. The author defines roughly 10,000 words over two years but notes funding ceased when no one evaluated the invention. He contrasts this with today's commercially produced AI and Anthropic, whose IPO values the company at $1.5 trillion while warning it could end all human life; he dismisses current AI as pattern-matching-based 'artificial neglect' rather than genuine intelligence.
items.title: A Radically Different Approach to AI

items.summary: Secure Solar Futures will build a 313-kW rooftop solar system of 531 bi-facial panels for Preston Park Elementary School in Roanoke, VA. Pardee Renewable Energy LLC funds most capital through a 25-year Power Purchase Agreement with no upfront cost to the school. In its first year the system produces 421 megawatt hours and will save $581,000 in net avoided electricity costs.
items.title: 313 kW Rooftop Solar System at Preston Park Elementary School

items.summary: Investors eye a rebound in Nvidia shares after the Financial Times reported that former chief executive Jensen Huang is discussing returning to the chipmaker, which has fallen 32% from its October high. Analysts Tim Waterer of KCM Trade and Anna Wu of Floodlines Research cite his exceptional track record amid market desperation for remedies.
items.title: Nvidia Shares Poised for Bounce Amid Jensen Huang Comeback Speculation

items.summary: Megaspeed International denies wrongdoing, calling itself a lawful business after reports link it to the downfall of Nvidia chief Jensen Huang. US officials allege former director Alice Huang (Huang Le) acted as a Chinese intelligence asset passing commercial information to Beijing; Singapore barred her from re-entry in 2025 and held her passport before releasing her for insufficient evidence, while Taiwan also blocked her. Megaspeed was once Nvidia's largest foreign chip buyer (~US$5bn over three years), incorporated in Singapore in 2015 as 7Road International. Its total assets rose roughly 90-fold to almost US$3bn by end-2024. Investigations span Malaysia, Singapore and the US; its global footprint remains puzzling.
items.title: Megaspeed Defends Legitimacy Amid Spy Allegations and Corporate Mystery

items.summary: On his penultimate day in Peru, Pope Leo XIV travelled into the Peruvian Amazon to demand justice for environmental defenders. He cited 57 murders between 2010 and 2024, calling on authorities to act against logging, illegal mining and coca-driven deforestation. The pope blasted impunity surrounding violence against Indigenous Awajún and Wampis schoolgirls in Condorcanqui province, where the Awajún and Wampis Women's Council recorded 370 cases between January and July.
items.title: ‘The blood of these brothers cries out’: Pope Leo demands justice for people killed protecting the Amazon

items.summary: More than 158,000 signatories, including Elon Musk, Tim Sweeney of Epic Games, Garry Tan of Y Combinator, and Uber co-founder Travis Kalanick, signed an open letter demanding the reinstatement of Jensen Huang as Nvidia chief. Over 7,500 identified employees—about 18% of the workforce—also joined. The letter follows Huang's resignation after revelations of extramarital affairs, one involving a woman accused of spying for China. US lawmakers from both parties have demanded that Huang and Nvidia appear before Congress to address national security concerns.
items.title: Tech Executives and Employees Rally Behind Jensen Huang's Return to Nvidia Amid Congressional Scrutiny

items.summary: India is returning toward interest rates last seen about two years ago amid accelerating inflation, rising food prices and geopolitical uncertainty. Economists expect the Reserve Bank of India to lift its benchmark rate by 50-75 basis points in coming months, reaching as high as 6.25% from 5.5%. Inflation breached the RBI's 6% tolerance ceiling in October, strengthening the case for further tightening after a first hike in nearly four years last month. Higher rates risk squeezing household demand and fueling political unease under Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government amid protests at their highest in a decade.
items.title: RBI Rate Hikes Ahead: Why Higher Borrowing Costs Could Hurt India

items.summary: Asian shares fell Monday after Jensen Huang's shock exit as Nvidia CEO, with the chipmaker's earnings and Anthropic's IPO set to test the AI-driven rally. Nvidia's market value tumbled from $5.8 trillion in early October to $3.9 trillion amid investor selling; analysts expect 90% revenue growth on $109 billion in its fiscal third quarter. Options imply a roughly +/-7% earnings-day move, though some question whether the numbers retain their usual significance as investors value Nvidia without Huang. Meanwhile, US producer and consumer price data nudged rate-hike odds higher, while Brent futures eased 0.2% to $95.69.
items.title: Asian Shares Fall Before Nvidia Earnings and Anthropic IPO

items.summary: Nvidia is under intense pressure amid a search for a new chief executive following the ousting of Jensen Huang. U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent demanded a dramatic shakeup in leadership, suggesting Nvidia look outside the company after accusations it facilitated sales of advanced AI chips to Chinese entities. The chipmaker faces scrutiny when reporting earnings on Tuesday, with some Huang backers campaigning for his return.
items.title: Nvidia Faces Pressure Over CEO Search as Bessent Calls for Leadership Shakeup

items.summary: The Indian rupee recovered from a March low of ₹96 to ₹93.63, its best level in six months, yet this may mask deeper weakness. While exports grew 23% year-on-year and FPI inflows reversed with $6 billion bought in ten days, the RBI's interventions—special dollar windows for Indian Oil Corporation, Hindustan Petroleum and Bharat Petroleum, higher repo rates, a Foreign Exchange Risk Reserve and USD-INR swaps—only eased demand without eliminating it. A strengthening US Dollar Index at an 18-month high and India importing roughly 90% of its crude oil in dollars threaten the recovery's durability. Last year's Economic Survey points to Germany, Japan and Switzerland as models where MSMEs built strong manufacturing exports; India must become more competitive rather than rely on currency-market intervention alone.
items.title: Has the RBI really stabilised the rupee?

items.summary: Apple is debuting a study app partnering with OpenEvidence to examine how people use clinically grounded health AI, rather than merely replicating chatbots. It invites U.S. iPhone 15-or-later users on iOS 26+ with Apple Intelligence enabled over age 21, aiming for up to 200,000 participants across more than 12 months. Users ask questions grounded in medical journals, rate answers, complete monthly surveys and share HealthKit data; OpenEvidence deletes query-response data after 24 hours, and the app won't train AI models. Apple cited OpenAI's report of over 300 million weekly health-related queries as motivation.
items.title: Apple launches new app to study how people use AI for health

items.summary: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent demanded a “dramatic shakeup” at Nvidia, questioning whether the company deliberately pursued illicit AI chip sales to China. Speaking on Fox News two days before its first quarterly earnings since Jensen Huang’s departure, he urged an external CEO and warned of compliance scrutiny.
items.title: Bessent Demands Nvidia Shakeup Over China Sales Concerns

items.summary: A United Launch Alliance (ULA) Vulcan rocket failed about 10 minutes after liftoff from Cape Canaveral on Sunday, destroying 40 satellites for Amazon's Leo internet network. The anomaly caused the first mission failure in ULA's two-decade history and disrupted plans to launch commercial service by 2026.
items.title: ULA Vulcan Rocket Fails Minutes After Launch, Losing Amazon's Leo Satellites

items.summary: Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang, now 63, weighs returning as CEO after resigning amid allegations involving a subordinate tied to China-linked Megaspeed. A Silicon Valley coalition backed by shareholders is lobbying the board for his reinstatement ahead of Nvidia's $4 trillion company's earnings release without him.
items.title: Jensen Huang's Nvidia Comeback Push Amid Scandal and Government Scrutiny

items.summary: In this Headstart On Record episode, career coach Jason Ho of Strengths School joins hosts See Kai Wen and Sue-Ann Tan to discuss identifying what suits you versus what you're good at. They explore striking a balance in your career, why some stay in draining jobs, the four personality archetypes, an ICE framework for finding your niche, and testing new interests without quitting.
items.title: Career Coach on Finding and Leveraging Your Strengths

items.summary: Over two days at COEX, more than 2,000 attendees converged for AI Day Seoul, gathering industry leaders, startups and developer communities focused on physical AI and agents. NVIDIA speakers Deepu Talla and Jonathan Cohen highlighted Korea punching above its weight as companies like Doosan Robotics, Hyundai Motor Group, LG Electronics, SK Group and Real World adopt NVIDIA platforms.
items.title: AI Day Seoul Unites Korea's Industry Leaders and Developer Communities

items.summary: Foreign portfolio investors posted their largest single-month inflow into Indian equities since November 2021, reversing earlier outflows of $2.17 billion (October) and $3.46 billion (September). Analysts cite lower crude prices—down ~21% to $93.37 from a $118 peak—and attractive valuations as drivers, though they caution the trend may be premature until oil and currency stability hold.
items.title: FPI Inflows Hit Five-Year High in November Amid Market Rally and Supportive Factors

items.summary: Technical analysts flag exhaustion in the Nifty near its 78.6% Fibonacci retracement at 25,475, hinting at a possible minor correction or sideways move before the next rally leg. Somil Mehta of Mirae Asset Sharekhán notes support around 24,700–24,800 and resistance near 25,424, while Dhupesh Dhameja of Centrum Broking points to an overbought daily RSI at 75.22 with heavy call open interest at 25,500 signaling immediate resistance.
items.title: Analysts See Nifty Consolidation Before Next Rally Leg Amid Overbought Conditions

items.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi is traveling to Manila for a two-day visit on November 16–17, attending the 23rd India-ASEAN Summit and the 21st East Asia Summit hosted by chairing Philippines President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. Bilateral trade between India and ASEAN stands at around $122 billion, making it one of New Delhi's major trading partners. Defense cooperation has gained momentum: in 2022, the Philippines became BrahMos' first foreign customer with a $375 deal for three shore-based anti-ship missile batteries. Discussions will cover maritime security, trade ties and AITIGA review, South China Sea dynamics under UNCLOS, Myanmar's role amid its 1,643-km shared border, and a possible Quad summit involving India, the US, Japan and Australia.
items.title: Modi's Manila Summit Visit and India-ASEAN Engagement

items.summary: India's government healthcare spending rose from Rs 1.3 lakh crore in 2013-14 to Rs 4.1 lakh crore in 2023-24, more than tripling over the decade. Meanwhile, households' direct share of total health expenditure dropped from 64.2% to 42.7%, though families still paid Rs 4 lakh crore out-of-pocket that year. Government healthcare spending accounted for just 1.43% of GDP in 2023-24.
items.title: Government Healthcare Spending Triples in a Decade While Household Burden Falls

items.summary: Helen Haines, an independent MP who lost both legs after being deliberately run down with a car outside her Wangaratta electorate office on October 19, has been discharged from the Alfred Hospital following four weeks and several surgeries. Suspect Brendan Nugent faces charges including dangerous driving causing serious injury.
items.title: Australian MP Helen Haines Discharged After Alleged Car Attack

items.summary: Dozens of garment factories across Savar, Ashulia and Gazipur closed this weekend after workers struck demanding a minimum wage of 30,000 taka (£182) monthly. The industry generates nearly $40bn annually but the current 12,500-taka wage is seen as insufficient amid rising living costs. Police shut factories under labour law's 'No Work No Pay' rule while unions clash over factory protection.
items.title: Clothing factories shut in Bangladesh as workers strike over pay

items.summary: Osaka prefectural police arrested Kentaro Kanao, a 33-year-old company employee from Hirakata city, on suspicion of abusing and killing his 3-year-old daughter Erena. His mother Riyo Kanao was also detained in Nisshin, Aichi Prefecture, for failing to respond appropriately as guardian by not reporting the father's behavior.
items.title: Man Arrested in Osaka for Alleged Abuse and Murder of Daughter

items.summary: This month's Black Friday and the January tax deadline are prime targets for fraudsters who impersonate genuine organisations to lure victims onto fake websites. HMRC received 95,340 suspected-scam reports in the year to October, including 900 involving malicious attachments directing users to counterfeit gov.uk pages. Lucy Pike of HMRC stresses that reporting scams helps shut them down.
items.title: Black Friday and tax return scams - don't fall for these

items.summary: Oil prices fell Monday as traders weighed a return to supply surplus after Middle East shipments through the Strait of Hormuz nearly recovered and US support measures eased fuel movement. Brent dropped 0.49% to $95.37; WTI fell 0.26% to $88.33, both lower than last week's declines. The IEA projects Q4 supply averaging 105 million barrels daily against demand of roughly 103 million, with emergency reserves releasing up to 71 million barrels by February.
items.title: Oil Prices Fall on Expected Supply Surplus

items.summary: For a common sample of 3,568 listed companies, aggregate net profit rose 26.2% in the September quarter versus 15.3% a year earlier, with revenue up 22.6%. Automobiles, financial services, oil and gas and metals drove gains while cement, FMCG and pharma lagged. Nifty 500 firms reported 26% growth against a 12% projection; large-caps led at 22.8%, midcaps moderated to 17.3% from 18.7%, and small-caps surged 42.3%.
items.title: India Inc Q2 Profit Jumps as Auto and Financials Lead Growth

items.summary: Indian banks propose a yield-based method to soften the impact of mandatory HTM bond revaluations under new accounting rules effective in 2027. Currently, falling bond prices hurt reserves and tier-one capital without affecting profits; since 60-80% of bonds sit in the HTM bucket, surging yields could hit banks hard. FIMMDA is expected to propose this method to RBI.
items.title: Banks Seek Alternative Accounting Plan for Bond Revaluation Blow

items.summary: Award-winning photographer Atong Atem presents her new solo exhibition, Passage, at the National Gallery of Victoria's Ian Potter Centre, becoming the first African Australian artist to have a solo show there. The high-contrast works explore postpartum experience, racist ethnographic tropes and enslaved histories through self-portraits that challenge how Black bodies were historically depicted without consent. Curator Natasha Bullock calls Atem a leading voice whose well-read vision gives the exhibition depth. Born in Ethiopia to South Sudanese parents, Atem relocated to regional NSW at six after time in a Kenyan refugee camp; she left architecture for painting and studied at RMIT. The scholarship that supported her included a $20,000 grant and 12 months of mentorship. Her career is defined by portraits subverting ethnographic stereotypes, drawing on her Dinka Bor heritage.
items.title: Atong Atem's Passage exhibition subverts colonial photographic history at NGV

items.summary: MidCoast Council became the first NSW council certified for large-scale managed retreat, ruling out costly seawalls and groynes at erosion hotspots like Old Bar. Manager Gerard Tuckerman said fewer than 20 homes are vulnerable now but several hundred could be at risk by 2100, with erosion averaging about 1 metre per year over decades. Residents face natural coastline movement without permanent protection. The council rejected a $147 million sand replenishment option that would have moved 1 million cubic metres of sand every decade. Other councils like Byron Shire and Port Macquarie Hastings are developing plans but not yet adopting retreat at scale.
items.title: NSW Councils Choose Managed Retreat Over Expensive Coastal Defences

items.summary: Iran struck an air base in Bahrain with six drones, the first direct hit on the Gulf state in weeks, amid conflicting claims of interception and impact. Iran says a path to ending its ninth-month conflict with the US remains open if Washington accepts Tehran’s conditions, though little signals agreement is near over nuclear and Strait of Hormuz issues.
items.title: Iran Strikes Bahrain Base; Path to US Deal Remains Open

items.summary: The India Meteorological Department reports a well-marked low pressure has intensified into a depression over the Bay of Bengal, moving north-northwest and likely strengthening into a severe cyclonic storm by November 17. Maximum sustained winds could reach 120-130 kmph, gusting to 145 kmph as it heads toward the Andhra Pradesh coast. Odisha has placed all districts on alert amid expected flooding, crop damage, and suspended maritime activities through November 20.
items.title: IMD Warns of Third Bay of Bengal Cyclone in Three Weeks

items.summary: On November 15th, 2026, the author released datasette-maplibre 0.1a0, a new Datasette geospatial plugin combining MapLibre GL with OpenFreeMap, a free vector map server run by Zsolt Ero. Most of it was built in one prompt to Claude Fable 5.2, drawing on datasette-cluster-map and datasette-leaflet-geojson plugins plus an openfreemap-demo.html file. A favorite feature displays SVG previews of GeoJSON shapes before loading WebGL previews as they scroll into view.
items.title: datasette-maplibre 0.1a0

items.summary: Activist Pranab Doley was arrested in July for protesting a proposed Hyatt hotel near Assam's Kaziranga National Park, spending 117 days under the National Security Act before the Gauhati High Court quashed it on November 6. He has long fought for Adivasi families—about 45 farming on a 19-acre plot of which 9.9 acres are earmarked for the project—who were evicted despite land titles. Doley says the Himanta Biswa Sarma government invoked the NSA to break him and deter other rights defenders, framing it as part of broader displacement across Assam's river islands, mining districts like Rabha Hasong council in Karbi Anglong and Dima Hasao, and over 1.5 lakh bighas parceled off from Dhubri to Sadiya.
items.title: Assam activist Pranab Doley on NSA detention and land struggles near Kaziranga National Park

items.summary: An 81-year-old citizen recounts an eight-month ordeal over persistent rainwater waterlogging in front of his home, which he frames as a case study of public grievance redressal. Beginning around September 2023 with verbal appeals to sanitary staff and shifting to written representations from October 2024 onward, he received only stock acknowledgements — “we will inform the concerned department” or “we will follow up” — for months without a complaint registration number. Only after repeated contact did his grievance enter the Public Grievance Redressal System (PGRS) with number 1008092500084, and later as VSP202608311937 following intervention by a journalist friend on August 31, 2026. Officials visited; the Zonal Commissioner promised resolution within three months that never materialized; budget sanction dragged through May–June 2026 before tendering began. On September 7 the system recorded his complaint as resolved even though waterlogging continued — a closure verified neither on the ground nor with complainant confirmation. The author argues administrative procedures are means, not ends: for an administration a file may close while for the citizen the problem persists.
items.title: How a System Works — or Does Not

items.summary: On November 15, 2026, the author advanced Datasette toward its 1.0 milestone, now 53% complete, aided by Claude Fable 5.2. The release prioritizes streaming support for TSV and CSV export via Response.stream(), adds security fixes including a GitHub advisory on private stored queries, introduces dozens of improvements such as copy-schema Web Components and JSON pretty-printing, and features CSS multi-page view transitions working in Safari and Chrome with Firefox 162 support expected by December 8, 2026. Bug fixes came from contributors Zihan Dai, Peter Olkhovets, Ilya Khalafi, and Ankita Advitot.
items.title: datasette 1.0a43

items.summary: The National Investigation Agency (NIA) launched an investigation on Monday into a network of overground workers operating in Jammu and Kashmir’s Pir Panjal region. These individuals allegedly provided logistical support, safe transit and ground-level assistance to terrorists of Lashkar-e-Taiba and Jaish-e-Mohammad in the area.
items.title: NIA Probes OGW Network in Pir Panjal

items.summary: The Kerala government approved the purchase of 24 Toyota Innova Hycross vehicles at an estimated cost of Rs 9.60 crore, sparking criticism given the state's financial difficulties. Chief Minister VD Satheesan had earlier stated that new cars were unnecessary and could be selected from the existing fleet. The decision has revived scrutiny of spending priorities and questions about whether such expenditure is justified under current circumstances.
items.title: Kerala Government's Rs 9.6 Crore Vehicle Purchase Draws Criticism Amid Financial Crisis

items.summary: The India Meteorological Department warned a deep depression over the west-central Bay of Bengal could become a severe cyclonic storm by November 17, then move toward Andhra Pradesh's coast within two days. Odisha has alerted its districts to prepare for what may be a third cyclone in three weeks, following Cyclones Arnab and Murasu.
items.title: Deep depression LIVE updates: Odisha steps up preparedness as IMD warns of another cyclonic storm over Bay of Bengal

items.summary: Prince William and Catherine will end their three-day Indian visit with a meeting of PM Narendra Modi in New Delhi, following the 2026 Earthshot Prize ceremony in Mumbai. The trip underscores deepening UK-India cooperation under Vision 2035, focusing on climate action, clean energy and economic growth. Each Earthshot winner receives £1 million (around $1.3 million). India has produced more winners than any other country since the prize began six years ago.
items.title: William and Kate's India Visit Highlights UK-India Climate Ties

items.summary: Aaryavir Sehwag, struck twice during his 58 off 61 balls and tournament top-scorer with 361 in five innings, recounted to his father Virender how India chased down Pakistan's 337 by one wicket on the final delivery—needing just 3 runs. Even Pakistani fans chanted 'Sehwag' from the stands as he hit the winning four.
items.title: Sehwag's son Aaryavir recalls India's last-ball Under-19 Asia Cup win over Pakistan

items.summary: The Special Investigation Team probing granite baron R Veeramani's alleged abuse of minors arrested a driver, Perumal alias Bala, on Saturday for bringing victims to him. This brought total arrests to 10 across nine cases involving 13 minor survivors. The arrest followed the ninth FIR filed on November 13 and included searches at his Royapettah residence.
items.title: Driver Arrested in Granite Baron Veeramani Sexual Abuse Case

items.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi is set for a three-day visit to Manila from November 16 to 18, attending the 23rd ASEAN-India Summit and the 21st East Asia Summit. India will prioritize maritime security cooperation in the Indo-Pacific amid ongoing disputes. At least 19 leaders are expected at the gathering under Philippine chairmanship of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN). A key issue is the Code of Conduct for the South China Sea, where ASEAN and China had provisionally agreed on approximately 80 per cent but remain divided over legally binding terms. Negotiations will continue under Singapore's future chairmanship in 2027.
items.title: Modi's Manila Visit and ASEAN Maritime Security Focus

items.summary: This episode of a video series on the Communist Party of China explores how officials balance decisive leadership with public consultation, warning against both commandism and tailism. It cites Chongqing's 2015 medical price reform, suspended within about a week amid opposition, Huangshi's majority-support elevator rule that installed 1,773 elevators benefiting nearly 100,000 people in two years, and China's poverty alleviation campaign lifting nearly 99 million rural residents out of extreme poverty from 2012 to 2020.
items.title: Balancing Decisive Leadership and Public Consultation in Chinese Governance

items.summary: This episode of a 12-episode video series examines how China's Communist Party combats corruption at every level, from top officials to grassroots cadres. Backed by 157 months of transparent disciplinary data, the approach targets both high-ranking "tigers" and petty offenders—"flies." In the first nine months this year, investigations began against 73 provincial or ministerial-level officials plus 79,000 village Party chiefs.
items.title: Setting the Rules Straight: Tackling Both 'Tigers' and 'Flies'

items.summary: Drug peddlers in Bhopal are increasingly using coded words and emojis to evade police surveillance while conducting drug transactions over WhatsApp, Telegram and other social media platforms. Suppliers avoid naming narcotics directly, instead referring to smack as 'ticket', marijuana as 'ghas' or grass, MDMA as 'happy pills', and ganja packets as 'pudiya'. Emojis signal the type of drug, quantity and payment.
items.title: 'Ticket' For Smack, 'Ghas' For Ganja! Bhopal Drug Peddlers Use Secret Codes, Emojis To Dodge Police Surveillance

items.summary: An IIM Indore study by Prof Manish Popli, published in the Asia Pacific Journal of Management, finds that firms with longer exposure to India's pre-1991 Licence Raj economy introduced 7.9% fewer new products after liberalisation. Analyzing manufacturing firms from 1993–2005, it shows industry dynamism weakened this effect while resource abundance strengthened it—suggesting reforms alone cannot guarantee innovation without overcoming inherited practices.
items.title: IIM Indore Study Links Licence Raj Legacy to Slower Indian Firms' Innovation

items.summary: A single faulty router may have triggered the nationwide ground stop ordered by the Federal Aviation Administration on Friday, highlighting risks from outdated infrastructure. The problem reportedly emerged while a contractor replaced copper wiring—conditions experts warned could reach unacceptable levels after a 2023 review. The transportation secretary called for $50 billion to prevent recurrence; an analyst likened aging systems to running a 30-year-old car.
items.title: Faulty Router and Aging Infrastructure Blamed in US Flight Stoppage

items.summary: Iran launched drone attacks against a US military base in Bahrain on Sunday, intensifying regional tensions even as Washington signaled reluctance to escalate. President Donald Trump reportedly may hold off striking Iran absent new provocations. Meanwhile, American assets continued arriving in the region, and three oil tankers caught fire after hitting naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz, which an Israeli analyst called inherently unstable.
items.title: Iran Attacks US Base in Bahrain as Talks Stall

items.summary: Humorist Dave Schilling opens by describing his holiday hibernation—sleeping until pitch black, snacking on cold pizza—and mocks grocery retailers' festive junk foods like Marks & Spencer's "picky bits" and Trader Joe's plain tubs. He then pivots to a darker premise: supermarket refrigerators in France were recently shut off remotely by Iranian hackers, with similar attacks elsewhere forcing food disposal. Schilling notes that internet-connected fridges from brands such as LG and Samsung let consumers adjust temperatures via smartphone apps—technology he views as solving a nonexistent problem while creating real vulnerability. His house has six rooms; his appetite demands 2,000-calorie tandoori chicken bites. He concludes by advocating ripping out the computers entirely in favor of backyard ice-and-food holes.
items.title: Why Would Anyone Want a Smart Fridge?

items.summary: The community union Acorn is leading direct-action campaigns against the cost of living crisis, forcing powerful institutions to negotiate directly rather than waiting for government intervention. Member Yasmin launched a national campaign after enduring unexplained water charges and a nine-month meter wait; United Utilities eventually credited £250 to her account. On 20 August, Acorn staged nine protests as part of its Dignity Not Debt campaign, compelling Yorkshire Water, Severn Trent, United Utilities and Dŵr Cymru Welsh Water into negotiations over bailiffs and AI use in debt collection. Members have also spent two years challenging Bristol council's bailiff practices, while Sam Kidel highlighted how £30 fines escalate through added fees.
items.title: Acorn's Direct Action Campaign Against UK Banks and Water Firms

items.summary: Cloud computing firm Megaspeed says alleged Chinese spy Alice Huang left in August 2025, amid an international scandal involving alleged ties to China's Ministry of State Security and a relationship with former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. Singapore's authorities probe the server export case but deny espionage charges; Nvidia has lost nearly $2tn since the story broke.
items.title: Megaspeed Says Alleged Chinese Spy Alice Huang Left Company Last Year

items.summary: A mysterious object, 1998 KY26, about 11 metres wide, shows non-gravitational acceleration unexplained by the Sun or Earth's gravity. NASA chief Jared Isaacman says it poses no known threat to Earth. Harvard astrophysicist Avi Loeb and colleagues Adam Hibberd and Adam Crowl suggest it could be Phobos 1, a Soviet spacecraft launched on 7 July 1988 that lost contact en route to Mars; they note KY26 reflects almost 52% of sunlight and rotates every 5.35 minutes. The dark comet theory lacks evidence for gas or tail, while other studies favor a dehydrated asteroid with solar radiation pressure as alternatives.
items.title: Mysterious Space Object KY26: Soviet Probe Hypothesis and Competing Theories

items.summary: On Nov. 13-14, drones reportedly struck three commercial ships near Romania's Black Sea coast, damaging one vessel and triggering fires aboard two others with no casualties reported. The Palau-flagged cargo ship Larissa 1 was hit about 12 kilometers (7.5 miles) from the Romanian coast near Sfantu Gheorghe while en route to Sulina. Defense Minister Stefan-Radu Oprea confirmed an investigation, amid a broader series of Black Sea attacks on shipping.
items.title: Drone Strikes Hit Commercial Ships Near Romania's Black Sea Coast

items.summary: On Sunday, Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei accused the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) of biased reporting on Tehran's nuclear program, blaming it on some managers' political approaches and influence from the United States and Europe. The charge followed an Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps strike using six drones against a US radar at al-Riffa Air Base in Bahrain.
items.title: Iran Accuses IAEA of US and European Influence

items.summary: This item compares recession chronologies for Germany from ECRI, the German Council of Economic Experts, Laurent Ferrara (2019), and employment-based measures. It notes that despite declining employment and hours in 2025-26, strong rising GDP makes a recession hard to argue, with the latest ifo nowcast for Q4 at 0.62% q/q.
items.title: Germany's Recession Chronologies and Q4 GDP Nowcast

items.summary: BJP spokesperson Pradeep Bhandari slammed Congress leader Rahul Gandhi over his absence from Parliament's Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas event honouring Bhagwan Birsa Munda. Bhandari claimed the boycott showed Congress hatred toward tribal and forest-dwelling communities, alleging Gandhi prioritises meeting 'agents of George Soros' in Hyderabad. Meanwhile, PM Modi virtually joined the celebrations from Gadchiroli, Maharashtra, inaugurating 246 development projects worth around Rs 3,000 crore.
items.title: 'Finds time for Soros agents, not Birsa Munda': BJP accuses Rahul Gandhi of snubbing tribal communities

items.summary: An IndiGo flight (6E 0623) carrying 192 people from Pune to Guwahati made an emergency landing at Pune airport shortly after take-off on Sunday morning. The aircraft's landing gear failed to retract, prompting the Indian Air Force to declare a full emergency and activate response teams. All passengers and crew remained safe as the plane touched down around 9:04 AM.
items.title: IndiGo Flight Emergency Landing in Pune After Mid-Air Gear Failure

items.summary: Alibaba Group launched its new flagship Qwen4-Max model, claiming performance that rivals Anthropic and OpenAI. The e-commerce giant scored near the top of coding benchmarks, outperforming Claude Fable 5.1 and Moonshot's Kimi K3.1 Pro. Alibaba kept the model closed-weight but plans smaller versions soon. Chinese firms including Alibaba, Moonshot and DeepSeek are challenging US AI dominance with rapid improvements in coding and reasoning.
items.title: Alibaba Unveils Qwen4-Max AI Model in Challenge to US Rivals

items.summary: Asian shares fell on Nov 16 after a volatile week marked by Jensen Huang's shock exit as Nvidia CEO, with the chipmaker's earnings (Nov 17) and Anthropic's IPO set to test whether the AI-fuelled rally continues. Nvidia's market value tumbled from about US$5.8 trillion in early October to US$3.9 trillion by Nov 13; analysts expect fiscal third-quarter revenue of US$109 billion with earnings growth of 90%. Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin are set to meet at the APEC forum in Shenzhen on nuclear arms reduction and the Iran conflict. Meanwhile, Fed minutes due Nov 18 focus attention on a possible December rate hike amid rising inflation data.
items.title: Asian Shares Fall Before Nvidia Earnings and Anthropic IPO Test Tech Rally

items.summary: Tata Motors PV revenue rose ~34% YoY to Rs 96,920 crore in Q2FY27 amid a net loss of Rs 5,531 crore. Jaguar Land Rover cut FY27 guidance to an adjusted EBIT margin of 2-3% and free cash outflow around £1.25 billion. Motilal Oswal holds a 'Sell' rating with a Rs 240 target versus the Rs 287 close, implying ~16% downside.
items.title: Tata Motors PV Shares Crack as Motilal Oswal Cuts Estimates After Weak Q2

items.summary: Nvidia's stock was little changed as the Financial Times reported co-founder Jensen Huang is discussing a possible return to the chipmaker, buoyed by backing from Silicon Valley allies including Altimeter Capital Management, Atreides Management and Tesla Inc.'s Elon Musk. Despite this optimism, shares remain down 32% from their October high amid AI-boom doubts. Analysts caution any rally depends on fundamentals ahead of Tuesday's earnings.
items.title: Nvidia shares steady after report on Jensen Huang comeback talks

items.summary: Shareholders sued US chipmaker Intel in San Jose, alleging it concealed a personal computer sales slowdown that triggered a nearly 29% one-day stock collapse on 30 October. The lawsuit, filed by Robbins Geller Rudman & Dowd against CEO Tan Lip-Bu and other leaders, claims false statements about depressed PC demand caused quarterly earnings to fall 9%, or roughly $800m, to $8.1bn.
items.title: Investors Sue Intel After Stock Plunge Amid PC Sales Slump

items.summary: Shares of India's Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles fell 7.5% at 265.9 rupees, the top loser on the Nifty Auto Index and Nifty 50 index, after cutting Jaguar Land Rover's fiscal 2027 core earnings margin to 2%-3% from a forecasted 4%. JLR contributes about 80% of Tata Motors PV's top line. The company now expects an outflow of £1.25 billion ($1.65 billion) this year amid weak China demand, MENA disruptions and restructuring costs. Systematix Institutional Equities cut its target price to 328 rupees from 330 while maintaining a buy rating.
items.title: Tata Motors PV Shares Fall After JLR Outlook Cut

items.summary: Asian stocks fell Monday amid lingering Nvidia turmoil after boss Jensen Huang, 63, resigned over extramarital affairs. Despite a reported bid for his return—backed by signatories including Elon Musk—the reinstatement trade stalled ahead of Nvidia's Tuesday earnings and the anticipated Anthropic listing. Investors also watched Xi-Trump-Putin talks at APEC in southern China.
items.title: Stocks Extend Losses as Traders Await Nvidia Earnings and Anthropic IPO

items.summary: The Wall Street Journal reported that the Trump administration plans to designate more than two dozen artificial intelligence national champions, including Nvidia, Amazon, Microsoft, OpenAI and Anthropic. The program aims to help these companies expand overseas and better compete with Chinese rivals. Reuters could not immediately verify the report.
items.title: Trump Administration Plans AI 'National Champions' Program, WSJ Reports

items.summary: On the penultimate day of his longest pontificate trip, Pope Leo XIV visited Peru's northeast rainforest to demand justice for environmental defenders killed protecting the Amazon. He referenced 57 murders campaign groups estimate occurred between 2010 and 2024, noting most killings go unpunished in Peru. Addressing sexual violence against Awajún and Wampis schoolgirls in Condorcanqui province, he cited 370 recorded cases from January to July alone. The 71-year-old Pope, recovering from lung cancer surgery, called for an economic model that respects the Earth rather than its irresponsible exploitation.
items.title: Pope Leo XIV Demands Justice for Amazon Defenders in Peruvian Rainforest Visit

items.summary: This NBER Working Paper by Bachas, Hoy, Jensen, and Shaukat examines tax fairness across income groups. Using data from 29 developing countries, they find horizontal inequities are as large as vertical equity issues and worsen with progressive reforms that burden wage earners more than the self-employed.
items.title: Horizontal Equity of Taxation: Citizen Beliefs and Policy Preferences

items.summary: Charles J. Courtemanche’s NBER Working Paper 36006 (2026) predicts the Health Resources and Services Administration rebate model pilot would cut covered entities’ net revenues by $1.5 billion, with full expansion to all of 340B raising losses to $22.8 billion—a 32% reduction—largely from administrative costs.
items.title: Projected Financial Impact of a 340B Rebate Model Pilot

items.summary: The US-led Pax Silica initiative, launched by under-secretary Jacob Helberg in December 2025, gained momentum as India joined the San Francisco Declaration alongside South Korea, Qatar and the UAE. Germany, Sweden, the Netherlands and the European Commission were expected to sign soon. The pact seeks shared responsibility for AI supply chain security amid China competition, Nvidia leadership uncertainty after Jensen Huang's exit, and concerns over AI spending sustainability ahead of a Trump-Xi meeting in Shenzhen.
items.title: US-India Sign Pact to Protect AI Supply Chain Amid Nvidia Row and China Competition

items.summary: At COP31 in Antalya on November 13, 2026, IEA Executive Director Fatih Birol praised China as a clean-energy superpower. In an interview with China Media Group, he said China's progress in solar manufacturing and deployment, wind power, battery storage and electric vehicles has impressed him over the past decade. He noted that intensifying geopolitical conflicts are prompting countries to accelerate energy transitions for security and economic reasons.
items.title: IEA Chief Hails China's Role in Global Energy Transition

items.summary: Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's scandal has stirred sadness in Taiwan, where deputy digital minister Isabel Hou said Sunday. Huang maintained close ties with Taiwanese tech firms annually. The controversy fuels Washington calls for tighter chip export controls amid his China lobbying and affair allegations involving Megaspeed, which denies smuggling chips to China. Taipei is aligning its export policy with the US as it seeks trusted partners.
items.title: Taiwan Deputy Digital Minister Responds to Jensen Huang Scandal

items.summary: A United Launch Alliance (ULA) Vulcan Centaur rocket suffered a mid-flight anomaly about 10 minutes after liftoff on November 15, destroying 40 of Amazon's broadband satellites. This marks the first outright mission loss in ULA's 20-year history and dealt a significant schedule blow to Amazon Leo — formerly Project Kuiper — as it competes against SpaceX Starlink. The failure underscores a massive scale gap: while Starlink operates more than 11,100 working satellites globally, Amazon has roughly 396 operational satellites in orbit.
items.title: ULA Vulcan Crash Destroys Amazon Leo Satellites; Starlink Maintains Massive Lead

items.summary: Millions of Australians were unable to use Outlook during a Microsoft outage lasting most of Friday, disrupting business and daily online activity. Experts say compensation is unlikely to cover lost productivity. RMIT Associate Professor Mark Gregory notes service level agreements may trigger credits if uptime targets—such as 99.49 per cent annually—are missed, but these typically return part of fees rather than offsetting downtime losses. Deakin IT lecturer Fariha Jaigirdar adds Microsoft only covers loss of service, not knock-on effects, with any credit likely a small discount on the next bill. The ACCC may act legally over telecommunications services, and Victoria Peak Litigation Funding is seeking class-action participants, though entitlements are unconfirmed.
items.title: Microsoft unlikely to compensate for loss of productivity

items.summary: Apple is developing the iPhone Duo 2, its second foldable smartphone, aiming to add features missing from the first model, including facial recognition. However, integrating Apple's familiar Face ID technology onto a foldable display proves difficult; prototypes exist but engineers continue working on integration. With hardware development approaching an important deadline, there is a possibility that this upgrade may not make it into the final product.
items.title: Apple's iPhone Duo 2 Faces Face ID Integration Challenges

items.summary: Jensen Huang is weighing a return as Nvidia's chief executive just four days after resigning from the company he co-founded and ran for 33 years. His resignation followed reports of extramarital affairs with Alice Huang of Singapore-based Megaspeed, accused of spying for China, and Kimberly Powell, an Nvidia vice president. CFO Colette Kress is now interim CEO as the $4 trillion chipmaker prepares Tuesday results. Allies are building a 'war room' to lobby the board, backed by shareholders Altimeter Capital's Brad Gerstner and Atreides Management's Gavin Baker through the 'Bring Jensen Back' letter signed by Elon Musk and over 8,000 employees—about 20% of Nvidia's roughly 42,000 workforce. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent urged a leadership shake-up within Washington.
items.title: Days After Resigning, Jensen Huang 'Talks' Return as Nvidia CEO

items.summary: Reports indicate former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has discussed returning to the company's top leadership, backed by Silicon Valley executives and employees lobbying its board. An online "Bring Jensen Back" open letter reportedly drew over 160,000 signatures, with support from figures including Elon Musk, Tim Sweeney, Garry Tan and Travis Kalanick. Meanwhile, Nvidia conducts an investigation into his departure while interim CEO Colette Kress prepares for quarterly results.
items.title: Huang eyes Nvidia comeback as supporters launch 'Bring Jensen Back' campaign

items.summary: In Pucallpa, Peru, Pope Leo condemned the exploitation of the world's largest rainforest, calling killings of tribal leaders 'murders' that must be solved. He warned against economic models exploiting nature for a few, noting Peru lost about 200,000 hectares of forest in 2025 alone. The trip drew his papacy's largest crowds—some 12 million people across a 12-day tour—with an estimated 500,000 lining his route in Cusco.
items.title: Pope Leo's Forceful Amazon Visit Amid Deforestation and Tribal Killings

items.summary: Background location tracking by retail and weather apps can silently drain your battery while building a profile of where you go. You don't need airplane mode; instead, shut down unnecessary trackers in Settings > Privacy & Security > Location Services. Scroll past map and ride-sharing services to other apps, then toggle off Precise Location at the bottom of each app's screen.
items.title: How to Disable Hidden iPhone Location Trackers That Drain Battery

items.summary: Influential tech executives are mobilizing support for Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang after his resignation, with Elon Musk and Epic Games' Tim Sweeney backing an open letter demanding the board reinstate him. Meanwhile, Nvidia's board explores successors—Arm Holdings' Rene Haas among them—and says its search is still early-stage as it investigates his departure amid personal-controversy reports.
items.title: Silicon Valley Allies Rally Behind Jensen Huang's Return

items.summary: A United Launch Alliance Vulcan rocket failed about 10 minutes after liftoff from Cape Canaveral on November 15, destroying all 40 Amazon Leo satellites and ending ULA's two-decade success streak. The fifth Vulcan flight since 2024, the loss struck Amazon's Project Kuiper network, which has deployed 398 of the 3,236 satellites needed for global coverage—roughly 12%.
items.title: Amazon's Vulcan Rocket Fails After Destroying 40 Satellites

items.summary: Global brokerage Jefferies reaffirmed Buy ratings across six Adani Group companies, projecting 23% CAGR growth in combined EBITDA and earnings through FY29. The conglomerate's planned $51 billion capital expenditure—nearly 28% of major Indian firms' capex—is concentrated in power utilities and infrastructure. Jefferies flagged elevated debt, project execution risks and cross-company financial exposure as key concerns.
items.title: Jefferies Bullish on Adani Group Amid $51 Billion Capex Plan

items.summary: A United Launch Alliance Vulcan rocket failed roughly 10 minutes after liftoff from Florida on its first mission in nine months, destroying a payload of 40 satellites for Amazon's Leo internet network. The BE-4 engines supplied by Jeff Bezos' Blue Origin are under investigation as possible causes, adding to setbacks that have delayed Amazon's efforts to rival SpaceX's Starlink constellation.
items.title: ULA Vulcan Rocket Fails Mid-Flight, Destroying Amazon's Leo Satellite Payload
