items.summary: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said Canada could turn to Chinese automakers if trade talks with President Donald Trump fail. Speaking in Cambodia ahead of a meeting with Xi Jinping in Shenzhen, he stressed Canadian auto workers must stay fully deployed in an integrated North American market. Any Chinese investment would require substantial manufacturing in Canada using domestic supply chains and critical minerals.
items.title: Canada Could Work With Chinese Automakers If US Trade Talks Fail, Says Carney

items.summary: Union Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal said India would get preferential US access with lower duties than competitors under a Trump-Modi framework. An interim February 2 deal would have cut Indian tariffs from a combined 50% to 18%, though that included a 25% Russian-oil levy. The Supreme Court struck down global tariffs on Feb 20, prompting a temporary 10% US tariff and leaving the final agreement uncertain.
items.title: India-US trade deal progress amid tariff uncertainty

items.summary: The APEC Business Advisory Council (ABAC) meeting is underway in Shenzhen, where members have expressed strong expectations for China to play a greater role in promoting economic integration across the Asia-Pacific. The council's participants are focused on deepening regional economic cooperation and see Beijing as central to advancing that agenda within the broader Asia-Pacific region.
items.title: ABAC Members See China as Key to Asia-Pacific Economic Integration

items.summary: In an exclusive CGTN interview, Michael Hart, president of AmCham China, discusses how dialogue can translate into tangible business benefits amid efforts to stabilize economic and trade ties. He highlights the organization's role in bridging policymakers and businesses through engagements in Washington, DC, while noting that China's market remains vital despite growing competition from Chinese companies.
items.title: AmCham China President on Stability for US-China Business

items.summary: Indian equity markets rose, with the Nifty surpassing 25,200 points. Banking, financial services and IT stocks led gains, while Eicher Motors, Asian Paints, TCS and Bharti Airtel were among key gainers. The rally tracked India-US trade talks following Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal's statements.
items.title: Indian equity markets rise as Nifty crosses 25200 amid trade talks

items.summary: On Monday, BJP MP Manoj Tiwari performed the Usha Arghya rituals of the four-day Chhath Puja festival in the Yamuna river in Delhi, accompanied by his wife Surabhi. Speaking to ANI after prayers, he said celebrations along the banks stretched about 15 kilometres and had grown significantly under the BJP-led government, which he credited for making arrangements—previously such gatherings were even prohibited. Weeks earlier, Tiwari claimed the Yamuna's pollution load had halved over a year due to cleaning works by the Rekha Gupta government. Prime Minister Narendra Modi extended greetings, calling it a confluence of faith and discipline. BJP chief Nitin Nabin performed final rituals with his wife Deepmala, praying for Bihar and the nation. Former minister Dharmendra Pradhan also offered arghya, extending blessings to devotees across Odisha, Bihar, eastern Uttar Pradesh, Jharkhand and Bengal.
items.title: BJP Leaders Perform Chhath Puja Rituals on Delhi's Yamuna Banks

items.summary: The BJP condemned Congress after a video showed party leader Devendra Yadav hurling a plastic bottle into the Yamuna, accusing it of polluting the river during Chhath Puja preparations. The government said cleaning drives are underway while thousands gather at Delhi ghats for rituals amid concerns over toxic foam and poor water quality.
items.title: 'Insult to faith': BJP shares video of Congress leader Devendra Yadav throwing plastic bottle in Yamuna

items.summary: Patrick Wong Fook Seng visited Marina Square on Nov 13 and found the mall quiet, though food outlets drew some customers while retail shops were nearly empty. He noted he is a man in his 50s who researches before shopping. Seeking a travel bag, he entered one prominent retailer where two sales staff ignored him despite greeting first; he left after about five minutes. Near eateries he visited three other travel bag shops with no customers present and again received no greetings or engagement, spending less than a minute each.
items.title: Poor Retail Service in Four Marina Square Shops

items.summary: A Lords national resilience committee report warns ministers are complacent about fast-changing, interconnected threats facing the UK and urges swift action to boost preparedness. The committee says most households remain unaware of risks from cyber-attacks, strikes on undersea cables and extreme weather despite Labour's Be Ready campaign. Supply chains pose particular danger: around 90% of the world's penicillin-type antibiotic base comes from China, with only one integrated facility in Europe; nearly 95% of UK retail food is supplied by nine companies across 131 hubs. BT has just two cable repair ships—one French-owned and unavailable, one UK-based but 35 years old. The report calls for a national resilience strategy within six months, an annual prime ministerial statement and emergency booklets for every household.
items.title: Lords Committee Warns UK Is Underprepared for Interconnected National Threats

items.summary: Twisted Sisters Thrift Store in Tunstall, which opened last week, invites customers and donors to nominate charities each month so donations rotate among organizations like City Dogs Home, Cancer Research and Diabetes. Owner Julie Rindam said the idea followed an eight-year charity shop that closed when its pastor retired; regular donors wanted to keep supporting causes. Manager Jeanette Worthington added the store also serves as a community hub offering free food, sanitary products, contraception and school uniforms.
items.title: Thrift Shop Asks Donors to Nominate a Charity

items.summary: The UK's zero-emission vehicle mandate requires 80% of new car sales be electric by 2030 and 100% by 2035, though Labour reportedly plans to reduce these targets. The climate change committee (CCC) will advise ministers on the effects this week. Campaigners warn weakening targets would harm consumers, noting petrol cars cost more than £100 to fill versus under £10 for electric charging. Greenpeace's Ami McCarthy and CCC chair Nigel Topping argue EVs drive industrial leadership and lower living costs. Conversely, Society of Motor Manufacturers and Traders chief Mike Hawes says manufacturers invest billions but face heavy discounts due to weak demand, urging fundamental target changes backed by consumer support.
items.title: UK EV Sales Targets Face Pressure Amid Industry Debate

items.summary: Martine Moise, wife of assassinated former Haitian president Jovenel Moise, registered as a presidential candidate. She was injured in the 2021 attack that killed her husband at their Port-au-Prince home and later flown to Florida for treatment; an assassination-related charge against her was overturned last year. Haiti's elections were postponed from December to July amid gang violence.
items.title: Widow of Assassinated Ex-Haitian Leader Registers for Presidential Election

items.summary: Sunday’s Fukuoka mayoral election ended without a winner after the record-breaking 13 candidates failed to reach the minimum legal threshold. The total vote count was 592,723 — 45.6% of eligible voters and 11.3 percentage points higher than the previous Kyushu region’s largest city election. The large number of rivals diluted the vote; only former Lower House member Shuji Inatomi came close with about 23%. A reelection will be held by Jan. 19.
items.title: Fukuoka Mayoral Election Ends Without a Winner

items.summary: Rui Muneyama won the Asia Professional Baseball Championship MVP over teammate Tomoya Masaki, ending a back-and-forth race watched by 36,000 fans. Manager Tadahito Iguchi playfully handed Masaki Japan's ¥30 million ($188,000) winner's check as consolation after Muneyama took the honor.
items.title: Samurai Japan's MVP Race Ends with Muneyama at LA Games Baseball Championship

items.summary: A teenage girl and her cat were reunited four days after a building in Brooklyn's Flatbush neighbourhood collapsed, forcing the family to relocate when part of their home was stripped away. City officials recovered the cat, Isaac, from the debris and shared the reunion Sunday afternoon. Eight people died and 18 others were injured in the three-storey collapse last Wednesday.
items.title: New York Teen Reunites With Cat After Building Collapse

items.summary: Jay Shah was elected unopposed for a second two-year term as chair of the International Cricket Council at its board meeting in Bali, per the ICC. He became the youngest ever chair when first selected in 2024 at age 35 and will oversee cricket's return to the Olympics at the 2028 Los Angeles Games. Shah is son of India's home minister Amit Shah.
items.title: India's Jay Shah Re-elected ICC Chair for Second Term

items.summary: A nearly three-year camera-trap survey (2021-2024) of the proposed Lundu Mangrove Protected Forest recorded the endangered flat-headed cat 59 times, mostly—49 detections—in nibong palm wetlands at 10 to 20 meters elevation. The cats avoided sea-level swamps and showed flexible day-night activity, prompting lead author Ahmad Ampeng of the Forest Department Sarawak to urge gazettement.
items.title: Camera-trap study reveals flat-headed cat's elevated-mangrove habitat preference in Sarawak

items.summary: A global study analyzed over 6,000 records of butterfly range shifts across 1,758 species in 105 countries. It found that 80% of surveyed species expanded their ranges while 27% contracted and 22% shifted along elevational gradients. Additionally, 79% of documented range shifts were associated with climate change or extreme weather events. Meanwhile, Sri Lanka experienced an unusually large butterfly mass movement in November 2026, driven by monsoon rains that boosted host plant growth.
items.title: Climate-Driven Butterfly Range Shifts and Sri Lanka's 2026 Mass Movement

items.summary: South-east Queensland faces a severe thunderstorm warning from the Bureau of Meteorology, with hail up to seven centimetres reported at Gatton, Lilydale and Heildon. A 91 km/h wind gust was recorded at Wellcamp Airport west of Toowoomba. Residents in Pittsworth described hail as heavy as snow. Storms are heading east across Ipswich, Somerset, Scenic Rim, Southern Downs, Toowoomba, Lockyer Valley, Gold Coast, Sunshine Coast, Brisbane City and Moreton Bay, plus the south-east coast, Central Highlands, Coalfields, Capricornia, Wide Bay-Burnett and Darling Downs. The SES urges safety precautions.
items.title: Severe Thunderstorm Warning Hits South-East Queensland With Heavy Hail and Strong Winds

items.summary: The inaugural Eurovision Song Contest Asia, held in host Thailand on November 14 with eleven countries competing, emphasized regional flavor through traditional dress and English-only delivery. Most songs were sung in artists' own languages (36%) or mixed with English (54%), versus the original contest's higher English share; only South Korea performed fully in English. The Philippines' Carmelle won at age 19 with Sobra-Sobra, earning 211 points across viewers from 183 countries and securing hosting rights for 2027. Thailand placed second on 169 points. While the event showcased diverse Asian pop beyond J- and K-pop, its longevity may depend on buy-in from Japan, China and India.
items.title: Eurovision Asia's inaugural diverse showcase and uncertain future

items.summary: Madhya Pradesh's Lokayukta searched three premises linked to Sanjeev Kumar Sharma, an assistant director at the Satpura Tiger Reserve. Teams seized ₹26.36 lakh cash, 2.5 kg gold valued at ₹3.5 crore and 1.6 kg silver worth about ₹2.9 lakh during a raid in Narmadapuram and Chhindwara districts on November 15.
items.title: Gold and Cash Seized in Raid on Madhya Pradesh Tiger Reserve Officer

items.summary: Mitsubishi Electric has unveiled The Little One, a compact residential air-to-water heat pump in its Ecodan range targeting new-build homes ahead of the UK's Future Homes Standard. Available from 2027 with propane (R290) refrigerant and A+++ efficiency, it comes in 4 kW and 6 kW versions achieving SCOPs of 4.77 and 4.65 at 35°C water flow. Weighing 58 kg and measuring 970×713×400 mm, the unit is 47% smaller and 40% lighter than a comparable existing model.
items.title: Mitsubishi Electric Unveils Compact 'The Little One' Heat Pump for UK New-Build Homes

items.summary: A Clean Energy Regulator report found that around 61% of inspected battery energy storage systems and about 23% of solar systems installed under the Small-scale Renewable Energy Scheme in 2025–26 were rated substandard, with less than 1% unsafe. Non-compliance stemmed almost entirely from poor workmanship rather than faulty products, prompting regulator communication with more than 830 installers.
items.title: Australian Regulator Rates Majority of Home Battery Installs as Substandard

items.summary: Bank of Japan board member Hajime Takata called for a nimble policy rate hike to reach a 'good' position near the median of staff estimates. The BOJ held rates at 1.25% last month, declaring victory in its fight against inflation and shifting focus toward preventing an overshoot above its 2% target as underlying inflation reached that level.
items.title: BOJ's Takata Urges Swift Rate Hike Amid Inflation Overshoot Fears

items.summary: Retail investors in India bought Rs 5,610 crore of HDFC Bank during the quarter, its largest purchase. Indian equities recovered in October after two months of negative returns: BSE Sensex gained 2.7% and Nifty 50 rose 1.9%, though mid- and small-caps fell 3.4% and 4.1%. Valuation premiums moderated—the mid-cap premium eased to 33% from 55%—yet remain elevated historically. Axis Mutual Fund favored quality large-caps, while PGIM's Vinay Paharia highlighted India growth pillars like financialization and capex.
items.title: Indian Retail Investors Buy Falling Stocks as Markets Recover in October

items.summary: Eicher Motors reported its highest-ever quarterly revenue of Rs 7,422 crore, up 20% YoY, with record EBITDA of Rs 1,760 crore rising 16%, though the margin slipped to 23.71% from 24.45%. Royal Enfield sold a record 3.77 lakh motorcycle units in Q2FY27, up 15% YoY. Shares jumped to Rs 7,947 on Monday. CLSA maintained its Outperform rating and raised the target price to Rs 8,670 from Rs 6,568 despite cutting FY27-28 EPS estimates by 1-2%. Jefferies retained a Buy call with a Rs 9,300 target implying 21% upside. MD B Govindarajan credited strong domestic and international demand for the record quarter.
items.title: Eicher Motors Posts Record Q2 Revenue and EBITDA as CLSA Raises Target Price

items.summary: Mirwaiz Umar Farooq, chief cleric of Jammu and Kashmir, was ranked among the world's 500 most influential Muslim personalities in The Muslim 500—2027 edition by Jordan-based RISSC—for a 13th consecutive year. Recognised for his religious leadership amid Kashmir's socio-political complexity, he leads Srinagar's Jamia Masjid and assumed the Mirwaiz role at 17 in 1990 after his father's assassination, later heading the All Parties Hurriyat Conference. His advocacy favours India–Pakistan dialogue, yet domestic restrictions persist: house arrest from August 2019 to September 2023 following Article 370's abrogation, plus ongoing curbs on prayer and calls for reviewing prolonged anti-terror detentions of Kashmiri youth.
items.title: Mirwaiz Umar Farooq Named Among World's Most Influential Muslims for 13th Year

items.summary: An Indian tech official said Indians view AI as less threatening than Americans, since fewer hold cognitive or office jobs that technology could replace. Young Indians embrace AI to boost productivity and lift India toward developed status within two decades, with gains in agriculture, education, healthcare and government. Around 6 million people work in IT-related services. A key constraint remains scarce, costly compute.
items.title: India Feels Less Threatened by AI Than the US

items.summary: Union Home Minister Amit Shah and Maharashtra Deputy Chief Minister Eknath Shinde held a 45-minute meeting in Pune amid speculation over defections from Uddhav Balasaheb Thackeray's Shiv Sena faction, dubbed Operation Tiger 3. Comments by Sanjay Shirsat suggested members might join the Shinde camp. Separately, ahead of Sonia Gandhi's memoir launch, the BJP criticized it as a self-goal seeking to whitewash history.
items.title: Shah-Shinde Pune Meeting Amid Shiv Sena Defection Speculation; BJP Criticizes Sonia Gandhi Memoir

items.summary: Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay is scheduled to fly from Chennai to Delhi by chartered flight before 2 pm Monday, returning by midnight after launching Congress leader Sonia Gandhi's memoir 'Belonging: A journey of love.' Opposition parties—DMK president M K Stalin and AIADMK chief Edappadi K Palaniswami—are urging Vijay to press the party leadership over Karnataka CM D K Shivakumar's remarks on building the Mekedatu dam, citing Supreme Court orders. The launch is restricted to invited guests.
items.title: TN CM Vijay set for Sonia Gandhi memoir launch amid Opposition's Mekedatu pressure call

items.summary: With about 98 percent of votes counted, President José Maria Neves is projected to win re-election in Cape Verde with nearly 64 percent of the vote. Claiming victory on Sunday evening, he pledged cross-party support for housing, healthcare and education plus job creation. His party PAICV won a parliamentary majority in May after more than a decade under the Movement for Democracy.
items.title: Cape Verde's Neves Projected to Win Re-election with Nearly 64% of the Vote

items.summary: Chief of Defence Staff General NS Raja Subramani outlined three shifts reshaping modern warfare at ANI's National Security Summit 3.0 in Delhi: changing economics, a technological contest led by the United States and China, and an expanding battle space. He warned that cheap drones now overwhelm million-dollar missiles, depleting US Patriot stocks rapidly, while front lines blur as entire nations become vulnerable targets.
items.title: CDS Subramani on Three Shifts Reshaping Modern Warfare

items.summary: Australia, Canada, Italy and the UK urged Israel to immediately allow 150,000 tents and supplies into Gaza before winter worsens a dire humanitarian situation. In Middle East tensions, USS Theodore Roosevelt joined two other carriers for three total US carrier presence; Iran struck Bahrain again after intercepting drones near Riyadh, while Saudi Arabia claimed destroying seven Houthi drones over Mecca, Medina and the Eastern Province—claims rejected by Houthis' Yahya Saree. Elsewhere, Ronaldinho returned to play 180 minutes...
items.title: Morning Briefing: Nov. 16, 2026

items.summary: Rashmi Barua argues that India's medal tally—21 golds at the 2026 Asian Games, matching Uzbekistan despite its smaller population—masks a deeper problem. She urges strengthening sport's base so more children want to play. Drawing on economists like Edward Deci and Uri Gneezy, she warns external rewards can crowd out intrinsic motivation, while incentives tied to what young people value work better. Barua notes barriers for rural schoolchildren and girls, cites regional football cultures in Manipur and Haryana, and calls for recognising effort over winning—so that children keep playing rather than dropping out of sport.
items.title: India's missing champions: why children must keep playing

items.summary: Hundreds of thousands of Czechs protested in Prague against a government plan to replace public media fees with direct state funding, which critics warn could undermine broadcasters' independence. Organizers estimate around 400,000 attended Sunday's demonstration, surpassing an earlier March protest and potentially marking the largest since the 1989 Velvet Revolution.
items.title: Czechs Rally in Prague Over Public Media Funding Plan

items.summary: The first-ever trilateral meeting of the presidents of China, the US and Russia is scheduled for November 19 as part of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit hosted by Chinese President Xi Jinping. Nuclear arms control, AI regulation and Iran are expected on the agenda, while Ukraine will be excluded from discussion. The world's two largest nuclear powers face binding limits after New START expired in February.
items.title: Trump, Xi, Putin set for historic trilateral meet in Shenzhen on Nov 19

items.summary: The US and nine partner countries signed the San Francisco Declaration on Sunday, November 16, 2026, under the Pax Silica initiative to secure critical technologies for advanced AI. Germany, Sweden, the Netherlands and the European Commission are expected to sign next week. The declaration precedes a planned Thursday trilateral meeting between Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen ahead of APEC.
items.title: US and Nine Partners Sign AI Supply Chain Agreement

items.summary: NAED Energy Holding Inc., a U.S. aerospace and utility-energy company, unveiled the PV-1 PECVD-V vertical in-line deposition platform for high-volume solar manufacturing. Combining plasma-enhanced chemical vapor and physical vapor deposition on one shared-carrier line, it targets 96,000 wafers per hour—double its previous XL-class throughput—and is engineered from day one to produce the T2X two-terminal perovskite/HJT tandem cell targeting 30% efficiency. NAED plans terrestrial and space markets with glass-glass modules starting at 600 W. Its intellectual property portfolio was appraised at $179 million under ASC 820 Level 3 methodology as of November 11, 2026.
items.title: NAED Unveils PV-1 Vertical Tandem Solar Platform

items.summary: Oil prices fell as the International Energy Agency warned of a return to oversupply, citing higher-price-driven demand cuts and Middle East supply recovery. On an annual basis, global oil supply would be 4.8 million barrels daily lower than in 2025, while demand declines only 2.7 million bpd. Goldman Sachs and JP Morgan also forecast gluts; Brent traded at $95.24 and WTI at $88.31 per barrel.
items.title: Oil Prices Fall Amid Return-to-Oversupply Fears

items.summary: PVH has developed a portfolio of advanced solar tracking systems and fixed-tilt structures combining adaptable mechanical designs, intelligent controls and digital monitoring to support efficient utility-scale power generation. Its AxoneDuo Infinity offers flexible configurations for diverse terrain with minimal motors per string, while Monoline 2P targets large-format modules via distributed slew-drive design. SolarFix provides cost-effective fixed-tilt options supporting 2P and 3P arrangements.
items.title: PVH Advanced Solar Tracking Systems Portfolio Overview

items.summary: On November 15, 2026, the author released datasette 0.65.6, backporting a minor security fix from version 1.0a43 that addressed an issue where databases with mismatched routes could be downloaded by unauthorized actors via / .db paths. The release page also lists recent articles covering topics including locating mysterious system sounds using Claude and evaluating Qwen 3.8 27B on personal hardware.
items.title: Datasette 0.65.6 Release and Recent Articles

items.summary: Sungrow hosted the Global Energy Pioneer Summit (GEPS) 2026 from November 10 to 13, gathering more than 1,200 guests from over 80 countries. The company unveiled POWER⁵, a five-pillar strategy guiding its global distributed energy business through product, marketing, partnership, service and ecosystem pillars. Sungrow cited 1,100 GW of cumulative installed capacity in power electronic converters and recognition by BloombergNEF as the world’s most bankable company across PV inverter, ESS and PCS sectors. President Simon Liu emphasized enhancing brand positioning for partner profit potential.
items.title: Sungrow Unveils POWER⁵ Strategy and Simplified Clean Energy Products at GEPS 2026

items.summary: During Chhath Puja celebrations in Delhi, devotees performed rituals amid thick white foam on the Yamuna. The Aam Aadmi Party accused both Delhi and central BJP governments of failing to clean the river, calling their claims false. BJP denied this, attributing the pollution to the previous AAP government and claiming the Yamuna is now more than half clean in just 2 years.
items.title: AAP and BJP Clash Over Yamuna's Toxic Foam During Chhath Puja in Delhi

items.summary: Chhath Puja concluded on Monday after four days, ending with morning arghya offered to the rising Sun. Devotees in Patna, Delhi, Gorakhpur, Kolkata and Ayodhya gathered at ghats for prayers. PM Modi posted greetings calling it a divine ritual of nature, praying to Chhathi Maiya for devotees fasting and his family across India. Leaders including Nitin Nabin, Samrat Chaudhary, Vishnu Deo Sai, Ravi Kishan and Manoj Tiwari performed arghya in their regions.
items.title: 'Pray to Chhathi Maiya to bestow her blessings': PM Modi extends greetings as festival ends with morning Arghya

items.summary: A United Launch Alliance (ULA) Vulcan rocket failed shortly after liftoff on Sunday, November 15, 2026, marking the launch company's first-ever mission failure. The vehicle lifted off from Space Launch Complex 41 at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida carrying Amazon's Leo satellites for its internet network; it suffered an anomaly roughly 10 minutes into the flight and destroyed its payload of 40 satellites. ULA confirmed that the Vulcan failed to deliver the Amazon mission to orbit, describing each flight as one that "teaches us something" while noting no specific data yet explained what occurred since the investigation was still underway.
items.title: ULA Vulcan Rocket Fails Mid-Flight, Destroying Amazon's Leo Satellite Payload

items.summary:
Jensen Huang is weighing a comeback as Nvidia's chief executive just days after his resignation over revelations of at least two extramarital affairs, one with a woman accused of spying for China. His allies in Silicon Valley are campaigning for his return even though an investigation into his conduct has barely begun. An open letter calling for his reinstatement has attracted more than 165,000 signatories, including Elon Musk, Tim Sweeney and Uber co-founder Travis Kalanick, with over 7,500 identifying as Nvidia employees—around 18% of the workforce if true. Meanwhile, the drama has knocked around $600bn off Nvidia's value so far. Colette Kress was named interim CEO last week, adding pressure ahead of her presentation of Nvidia's latest financial results tomorrow afternoon.

Nvidia's shares are down almost 2% in premarket trading at $159. 67—about 14% below their level just over a week ago before the news broke.
items.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's Possible Return Amid AI Sell-off and Global Market Moves

items.summary: The European Central Bank reported on Monday that failures at external technology providers have become a larger source of tech problems for euro zone banks than fraud attempts. In its Financial Stability Review, the ECB noted that malicious actions accounted for only a relatively small share of major cyber incidents affecting these banks between the start of 2025 and September 2026, with most such incidents having limited impact. By contrast, roughly one‑fifth of cyber incidents stemmed from third‑party providers used by banks—especially those supporting their IT systems—and this reliance created problematic dependencies because many large providers are based outside the European Union.
items.title: ECB: Outsourcing Is a Bigger Risk Than Scams for Euro Zone Banks

items.summary:
Jensen Huang, co-founder and former chief executive of Nvidia who resigned last week following multiple extramarital affairs—including with an alleged Chinese spy—is reportedly eyeing a comeback. According to a report by the Financial Times, Huang discussed with confidants the possibility of returning to his post as a long-admired figure in artificial intelligence who once rose to international stardom. A Huang ally told the publication that allies are assembling a “war room” of Silicon Valley executives to lobby for his reinstatement, with tech leaders actively supporting the effort.

However, not everyone is aligned with Huang’s return.
items.title: Elon Musk joins calls to bring back Jensen Huang as allies build 'war room' to lobby his return

items.summary:
A former Hobart teacher, Stephen Fane Noga (76), was successfully sued by one of his former students for allegedly sexually abusing her in the 1980s. Earlier this year he was taken to court by a former student from Hobart Matriculation College—now aged in her 60s—who alleged repeated sexual abuse, and who also sued the State of Tasmania for failing its duty of care. Justice Stephen Estcourt found in favour of the terminally ill woman, awarding her a cumulative $1.

In May, Mr Noga's legal team launched an appeal against Justice Estcourt's decision on four grounds.
items.title: Tasmanian Judge's Facebook Activity Not Enough to Undo Decision Against Teacher

items.summary:
According to reports, Apple is preparing to introduce three new iPhones—the iPhone 18, the budget-oriented iPhone 18e, and the ultra-slim iPhone Air 2—between February and April 2027. The company has not officially confirmed these launch dates, though the shift may be linked to its foldable iPhone plans. Rather than a traditional September release, Apple could roll out different models at separate times, potentially changing when buyers decide to upgrade.

The standard iPhone 18 is expected to feature a 6. 3-inch LTPO OLED display with 1. 5K resolution, thinner bezels, and brighter visuals.
items.title: Apple's 2027 iPhone Refresh: Staggered Launches and Rising Prices

items.summary: The District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission in Malappuram ordered Samsung India Electronics Pvt Ltd to pay a consumer named Sakeer V P after his air conditioner became unusable because the defective circuit board could not be replaced due to unavailability of the spare part. The order was passed on October 30, 2026, following a complaint filed by Sakeer, who purchased a Samsung AR12NV3JGMCNNA AC from Shajahan T V & Fridge House-2016 in Perinthalmanna on August 6, 2018 for Rs 39,000.
items.title: Kerala Consumer Commission Orders Samsung to Pay Rs 20,000 After AC Repair Failure

items.summary: Samsung has increased the prices of select models from its Galaxy M and F series for buyers in India. The company reportedly revised the listed prices of all seven configurations of the Galaxy M17 5G, Galaxy M17e and Galaxy F70e 5G by ₹2,000 each. These changes cover both dealer and list prices and are inclusive of GST. The revision took effect on November 15, 2026, according to a Samsung price-revision circular shared by tipster Sanju Choudhary on X. The update affects different RAM and storage configurations across the three models, with some variants now crossing the ₹25,000 mark as a result of the increase.
items.title: Samsung Raises Prices on Galaxy M17, M17e and F70e in India

items.summary:
Anthropic is pursuing a proposed initial public offering valued at around $1. 4 trillion, with plans to put 825 million Class A shares on the market at $70-78 apiece following an amended registration statement filed November 10. At the upper end of that price band, the offering could fetch approximately $64. 35 billion and place Anthropic's fully diluted valuation near $1. 4 trillion — above its $965 billion May funding round but below the roughly $2 trillion it reportedly aimed for earlier this year. Shares would trade under the ticker ANT.

The listing arrives amid sharply contrasting returns from recent technology IPOs, per an S&P Global Market Intelligence analysis of seven major US listings: four traded above offer prices a year after listing while three suffered losses. Arm Holdings led with a 171. 4% return after its September 2023 debut; Snowflake and Airbnb gained 169. 6% and 165. 3%, respectively, followed by DoorDash at 61. 6%.
items.title: Anthropic's Proposed $1.4 Trillion IPO Amid Uneven Tech IPO Returns

items.summary:
A ranking of the most-followed personalities on Instagram across Asia, based on follower counts, places cricket legends, global leaders, Bollywood icons and K-pop superstars among its top names. Virat Kohli leads the list as Asia’s most-followed personality, followed by Narendra Modi and BLACKPINK’s Lisa. Priyanka Chopra Jonas ranks among the highest-placed Indian names on the chart, while Katrina Kaif secures the 10th position with 78. 6 million followers. Other featured names include Shraddha Kapoor, Alia Bhatt, and BLACKPINK members Jennie, Rosé and Jisoo.

The ranking underscores the massive social-media reach these personalities command across Asia and beyond.
items.title: Priyanka, Katrina Join Virat Kohli, Modi Among Asia’s Most-Followed Instagram Stars in 2026

items.summary: Microsoft released emergency out-of-band updates to resolve Windows activation and licensing failures triggered by the month's security updates. The company confirmed via a Wednesday service alert that the issue affects organizations using the Software Licensing Management Tool (SLMGR) command-line tool to automate Windows activation and licensing processes. Enterprise customers who do not use SLMGR for licensing management but have the KMS client key installed in their image are unaffected, as devices already activated remain activated.
items.title: Microsoft Emergency Windows Updates Address Activation Failures From Recent Security Patches

items.summary: A report indicates that Jimmy Naval Tata, younger brother of the late Ratan Tata and one of three perpetual trustees of the Sir Ratan Tata Trust (SRTT), has sided with Tata Sons chairman N Chandrasekaran against his half-brother Noel Tata amid an ongoing struggle over control of the Tata Group. Conveying his views in a documented communication to fellow trustees, Jimmy described Chandrasekaran as a "proven star performer" who improved group earnings, reduced debt and delivered higher dividends, while expressing disappointment at the lack of trust leadership support compared with the backing JRD Tata gave operating heads.
items.title: Jimmy Tata Aligns with Chandrasekaran in Tata Group Succession Battle

items.summary: A woman is alleged to have stolen gold and diamond jewellery from a house in Akkayyapalem, within the jurisdiction of the Fourth Town Police Station in Visakhapatnam. According to a family complaint, she had befriended one member through Instagram before visiting their home. Claiming to be unwell, she reportedly stayed at the residence for several days and gained the family's trust. Taking advantage of this situation, she allegedly stole gold and diamond ornaments from a cupboard (bureau) in the house and fled. The stolen items reportedly include an 11. 3-gram diamond necklace along with other gold jewellery.
items.title: Woman Allegedly Steals Gold and Diamond Jewellery After Befriending Family on Instagram in Vizag

items.summary: This NBER Working Paper (36009, 2026) by Emanuele Colonnelli, Timothy McQuade, Natalia Rigol, and Benjamin N. Roth investigates whether firms benefit privately from measuring impact—despite impact measurement being central to impact investing and social entrepreneurship while little is known about private benefits of such measurement. The authors conduct the first randomized controlled trial of an impact measurement intervention among high-growth social enterprises in India. Treated firms exhibit nearly twice as much revenue growth and raise nearly twice as much capital as control firms, indicating that impact measurement can shape firm growth and capital allocation.
items.title: Measuring the Impact of Impact Measurement -- by Emanuele Colonnelli, Timothy McQuade, Natalia Rigol, Benjamin N. Roth

items.summary: In this NBER Working Paper 36008 (2026), Bruce C. Greenwald and Joseph E. Stiglitz use the Phelps-Winter customer-market framework to argue that raising interest rates induces higher prices, contrary to conventional expectations. They contend firms value current profits more heavily in a customer-market structure and are therefore more willing to sacrifice customers for short-term gains. As a result, rate hikes can be inflationary even when they succeed in cutting aggregate demand.
items.title: Monetary Policy in a Phelps–Winter Economy (Greenwald & Stiglitz)

items.summary: Shares of Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles fell more than 9 percent on Monday after the automaker reported a consolidated loss of Rs 5,531 crore for the September quarter. The stock dropped 9.23 percent to Rs 260.50 on the BSE and 9.41 percent to Rs 260.35 on the NSE. This followed a year earlier when the company reported a consolidated profit of Rs 76,170 crore in the corresponding quarter. The loss was driven largely by exceptional items totaling Rs 6,738 crore, which included employee separation costs of Rs 3,776 crore and asset impairment making up another Rs 2,856 crore.
items.title: Tata Motors PV Shares Slide After Q2 Loss and JLR Guidance Cut

items.summary: Nashik authorities reported that a fake Instagram account impersonating the official social media platform of the Nashik-Trimbakeshwar Kumbh Mela Authority has come to light, raising concerns about misleading devotees and citizens. During routine cyber patrolling on Nov 15, police detected an Instagram account operating under the handle official. kumbhnagari_nashik, which was publishing reels and posts related to the upcoming Simhastha Kumbh Mela 2027. The account's name and presentation created the impression that it was an official platform of the Kumbh Mela Authority, potentially misleading users. Nashik City Cyber Police have registered a case at Nashik City Cyber Police Station under Crime Register No.
items.title: Fake Instagram Account Impersonating Kumbh Mela Authority Detected in Nashik; Cyber Police Register Case

items.summary: The Indonesian rupiah fell to a fresh record low of 18,271 per US dollar on Nov 16, dropping as much as 0. 4% amid a stronger dollar driven by hawkish expectations from the US Federal Reserve about faster interest rate hikes. Over 2026, the currency has weakened roughly 9%, underperforming regional peers and reflecting investor concerns over domestic political stability. These worries stem from President Prabowo Subianto's policy uncertainty, the exits of several key policymakers, and Vice-President Gibran Rakabuming Raka's recent resignation, alongside MSCI's warning that it could downgrade Indonesia's equity market to standalone status.
items.title: Indonesian Rupiah Hits Record Low as Stronger Dollar and Fed Hike Bets Pressure Currency

items.summary: Cybersecurity firm AAA Technologies announced on Monday that its board has approved the establishment of four wholly-owned subsidiaries to expand operations overseas. Three entities—located in Singapore, Mauritius and Dubai—are intended to carry its cybersecurity and audit business abroad: AAA Technologies Singapore Pte Ltd (proposed share capital up to SGD 5 lakh), AAA Technologies Mauritius Limited (capital commitment up to $5 lakh, pending a Global Business Licence from the Financial Services Commission of Mauritius) and AAA Technologies MENA FZCO in Dubai's DMCC Free Zone (up to AED 10 lakh).
items.title: AAA Technologies Approves Four Overseas Subsidiaries and Semiconductor Design Foray

items.summary:
A Lashkar-e-Taiba terrorist was killed during an encounter with security forces on Monday, according to police sources. The counterterror operation took place in Jammu and Kashmir's Kulgam district, where the whole area was cordoned off to prevent the suspected terrorists from escaping. Security forces launched the operation following intelligence inputs about the presence of terrorists in the region.

The encounter occurred days after an attack on CRPF personnel left three security personnel injured. Further details about the deceased were not immediately available, as authorities awaited recovery of the body and confirmation of his identity before sharing information publicly.
items.title: Lashkar-e-Taiba Terrorist Killed in Kulgam Encounter Days After CRPF Attack

items.summary: Belrise Industries Limited (BIL), an integrated automotive component manufacturer, reported growth in both revenue and profitability for Q2 FY27 and the first half of FY27. Company-wide revenue from operations rose 17% year-on-year to Rs 2,746 crore in Q2 FY27, up from Rs 2,353 crore a year earlier; profit after tax (PAT) increased 25% to Rs 166 crore from Rs 133 crore. Manufacturing revenue grew 26% YoY to Rs 23,441 million in Q2 FY27 versus Rs 18,601 million the year-ago quarter, and manufacturing EBITDA rose 19% to Rs 3,170 million from Rs 2,663 million, with a margin of 13. 5%. Over H1 FY27, manufacturing revenue increased 23% YoY to Rs 45,420 million against Rs 36,923 million in H1 FY26; manufacturing EBITDA rose 15% to Rs 5,963 million from Rs 5,199 million at a margin of 13. 1%. Management noted that 71% of manufacturing revenue came from powertrain-neutral products during both periods.
items.title: Belrise Industries Q2 FY27 Results: Profit and Revenue Growth on New Orders

items.summary: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney warned that Ottawa could look to Chinese automakers for support should negotiations with U. S. President Donald Trump fail to safeguard an integrated North American car industry. Speaking at the Francophonie Summit in Phnom Penh, Cambodia on Monday, Carney said Canada's auto workers—whom he called “the best in the world”—should be fully deployed across a continental market that has grown less integrated due to U. S. trade actions. He maintained that talks with Washington remain his priority, but cautioned their outcome could determine whether Canada turns instead to European, Chinese or Japanese manufacturers.
items.title: Canada ready to turn to Chinese carmakers if US trade talks fail to protect auto sector, PM Carney says

items.summary: The Supreme Court on Monday suspended the life sentences of two convicts, Bipin Chandra Joshi and Pradeep Mordhiya, in the Bilkis Bano gang-rape and murder case and granted them bail. In its October 28 order, a bench comprising Justices M. M. Sundresh and P. B. Vohra noted that the two appellants had been under incarceration for more than 17 years, adding that one of them has a severe handicap. The court stated it would suspend the sentence and grant bail on such terms and conditions as may be imposed by the concerned trial court.
items.title: Bilkis Bano gang-rape and murder case: SC suspends life sentence of two convicts, grants bail

items.summary: Inox Wind shares fell to Rs 58. 01 apiece on the NSE on Monday morning, marking a sharp decline following disappointing second-quarter results for fiscal year 2027. The renewable energy company reported a consolidated net profit of Rs 58. 83 crore for the July-September quarter, down around 36% year-on-year from Rs 91. 75 crore in the corresponding period of FY26. Revenue from operations rose more than 21% YoY to Rs 1,354 crore against Rs 1,119 crore a year earlier, while total expenses climbed more than 28% YoY to Rs 1,275 crore. EBITDA dropped more than 22% YoY to Rs 238 crore from Rs 306 crore in Q2 of FY26, with the EBITDA margin slowing to 17%. The company noted that these figures do not reflect its true picture because income from its WindWorld O&M portfolio has not been recognised for the quarter.
items.title: Inox Wind shares tumble 10% as Q2 margins disappoint, CEO resigns. Why Motilal Oswal cut target price, earnings estimates

items.summary: A Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson announced Monday that Chinese President Xi Jinping will hold the China-Russia-US Summit together with Russian President Vladimir Putin and US President Donald Trump. The summit is scheduled for November 19, a date explicitly stated by the source as when the meeting will take place. The event is set to occur in Shenzhen, located in south China's Guangdong Province. A cover image accompanying the announcement shows an aerial view of Nanshan District in Shenzhen, dated August 19, 2026, attributed to VCG.
items.title: Xi to Hold China-Russia-US Summit with Putin and Trump in Shenzhen on November 19

items.summary: This piece reflects on a fishing community's enduring relationship with the sea and its families' tradition of waiting. For generations, fishermen have left Tanmen to work at sea, while their families learned to wait for their return. The article notes that today another generation continues going out to sea, as those who remain at home watch the horizon in anticipation of their coming back. It emphasizes that for these people, the sea is not merely a means of making a living but also where family stories begin. One family still carries the memory of a fishing disaster more than half a century ago.
items.title: The Sea We Call Home — Part Five: Waiting for the Boats to Return

items.summary: A Guardian politics live bulletin opens by flagging two issues expected to dominate the week: an EU reset and the Alan Milburn report on youth unemployment, for which the BBC reports that employer national insurance for workers under the age of 25 should be cut. On the EU front, Andy Burnham — referred to as the prime minister throughout — is due to agree a deal at a summit on Friday and has set out three tests any agreement must pass: it must remain consistent with the manifesto and government red lines; improve upon the Brexit deal rather than pursuing the hard Brexit never seriously argued for in 2016; and pass the Makerfield test by delivering tangible improvements, especially cutting business costs, easing consumer prices and creating opportunities for young people.
items.title: Ed Miliband defends doing 2015 election interview with Russell Brand, saying he was ‘taking him on’ not endorsing him – UK politics live

items.summary: Canada has been closely assessing the midterm election results in its southern neighbor and gauging what they may mean for relations between the two countries. Among many Canadians there is a general feeling of cautious optimism, while some Democrats in the U.S. have indicated that they want to end tariffs with Canada. The article frames these developments as an open question about how the midterm outcome will shape future bilateral ties, reported by CGTN's Nina Devries.
items.title: Canada Weighs Impact of US Midterm Elections on Bilateral Ties

items.summary: Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese is preparing for a Tuesday meeting with US President Donald Trump, in which he aims to balance his relationship with Washington while advocating for a swift resolution to the wars in Iran and Ukraine. He will urge the United States to deepen its engagement in the Indo-Pacific region. The summit takes place against a backdrop of significant diplomatic activity: it is set to be Trump's first Quad leaders' summit, whether during either of his presidencies, as he prepares for historic three-way talks with China's Xi Jinping and Russia's Vladimir Putin this week. Underpinning Australia's diplomatic posture are efforts by the federal government to avoid alienating China, particularly following a 2024 agreement on new protections around key AI technologies. That accord—the San Francisco Declaration—was designed to strengthen supply chains for chips and critical minerals while promoting cooperation amid concerns about Beijing controlling areas of AI development.
items.title: Albanese treads tightrope in upcoming Trump meeting, wanting Indo-Pacific engagement and end to Iran and Ukraine wars

items.summary:
The Duke of Sussex made a surprise two-day visit to Ukraine to support injured war veterans, arriving under a press blackout for security reasons while the country continues to face missile attacks from Russia. In Lviv he was greeted with emotional scenes and applause by wounded service men and women, telling his audience: "You're going to win the war." He described Ukraine as experiencing elements of war that no other country has faced before, noting advances in drone warfare alongside developments in protecting cities and providing treatment.

Ukraine now reports more than 150,000 injured war veterans. At the Superhumans Center near Lviv, Harry saw how growing numbers of injured veterans receive groundbreaking treatment, including an innovation for Mykhailo Damaskin, a Ukrainian air assault forces veteran who was so seriously wounded in Kherson that he was never expected to walk again.

The article was published under a security-related press blackout until Harry had left Ukraine.
items.title: 'You're going to win the war': Harry praises war veterans on surprise Ukraine visit

items.summary: The UK, Australia, Canada and Italy issued a joint statement urging Israel to "allow immediate, rapid and unimpeded humanitarian access throughout Gaza", describing the situation on the ground as "dire". The foreign ministers warned that recent floods have brought further suffering to the war-torn territory following its first winter storm, with 150,000 tents and other vital supplies being held at the border. Israel's military authority, which controls the Gaza crossings, said it is co-ordinating with the US-led Board of Peace and the UN on a winter plan, reporting that 93,000 tents and 8,600 aid trucks carrying winter supplies had entered the territory.
items.title: UK and allies call on Israel to allow rapid humanitarian access to Gaza

items.summary: On November 14, thousands of climate activists, trade unionists and civil society campaigners filled the streets of Antalya, Türkiye, turning a rainy day into a large demonstration for climate justice during COP31, the ongoing UN climate conference. The march opened the People's Climate Summit, a parallel gathering held from November 14 to 18 that organisers say will involve more than 130 organisations in around 150 events with participants from 34 countries. Protesters challenged fossil fuel dependence, corporate control of natural resources, forest destruction and climate inequality, calling not only for emissions cuts but also public control of energy, workers' rights, climate finance and accountability for polluters. The article stresses that the movement's concerns have widened: banners demanded an end to fossil fuels, protection of forests from commercial exploitation and greater community say over land, water and energy.
items.title: Climate Movement Expands Its Demands at Türkiye Summit in Antalya

items.summary: A letter writer from Worthing, West Sussex reports that the Department for Work and Pensions (DWP) is knowingly paying her too much local housing allowance due to a recognised system defect. Under 35 and claiming universal credit, she is entitled to shared accommodation allowance of £586 a month, but has instead been receiving the higher one-bedroom rate for couples at £790 a month for the past 18 months — an overpayment of more than £3,600 and counting.
items.title: DWP system glitch overpays housing allowance and risks partner's immigration status

items.summary:
Ng Yin Hong, a 56-year-old Singaporean former project manager with EM Services, was sentenced on Monday (Nov 16) to eight months and two weeks in jail after pleading guilty to corruptly accepting gratification. Ng had been employed by the managing agent of West Coast Town Council from 2001 to 2024 under contracts administered by EM Services, a company established in 1988 as a joint venture between Keppel Land Limited and the Housing and Development Board. In late September 2022, West Coast Town Council published an advertisement inviting tender bids for a re-roofing project covering 41 blocks in Teban Gardens, Pandan Gardens, West Coast Drive and Jurong West, valued at S$3. 3 million. Ng was the contact person for those interested to place bids.

The contract for the 41-block re-roofing project was signed in March 2023 and completed in July 2024 with a final value of about S$3.
items.title: Singapore Project Manager Sentenced for Accepting S$50,000 Bribe on Town Council Tender

items.summary: Overnight in a barrage Ukraine fired at least 1,336 drones toward Moscow, according to Russia's defence ministry — described by AFP as the second-highest daily figure of the year. Around 600 were intercepted near the capital before striking the Crimean bridge that links the annexed peninsula to mainland Russia; Russian-installed officials reported only minor damage and restricted traffic until afternoon, without confirming any casualties.
items.title: Ukraine's 1,336-Drone Strike on Russia's Crimea Bridge and the Shenzhen Summit

items.summary: The article argues that U. S. allies across North America to Europe and East Asia are increasingly afraid of the United States itself, rather than authoritarian China, which for years was regarded as the predatory nation they sought to de-risk from. These countries recognize that attempting to fully decouple from a powerful but predatory power would be ruinously expensive or futile; yet out of concern for their security and sovereignty, they feel compelled at least to pursue de-risking strategies. The urgency of this concern has grown following recent U. S. midterm elections.
items.title: U.S. Allies Fear De-Risking from America After Midterm Elections

items.summary: The article reflects on Jonathan Swift's 1726 satire, Gulliver's Travels Into Remote Regions of the World, arguing that it takes rare genius to write a work still read three centuries after publication. While most satire dwells on soon-to-be-forgotten figures and details, Swift produced something more enduring: a piece far more relevant today than when he wrote it amid powdered wigs and knee breeches. The third part of the masterpiece focused on remote regions governed by scientists, technologists, and projectors—technicians who were an isolated species in Swift's era.
items.title: Gulliver visited our AI world 300 years ago. He left in disgust.

items.summary: Across the Carolinas and other states this month, Democrats routed incumbent Republicans partly because voters feared an onslaught of AI data centers that threaten to drain water supplies, increase climate and air pollution, and drive up energy costs. The backlash extended beyond elected officials: in both red and blue areas, voters approved dozens of ballot measures pausing or restricting such facilities, adding to more than 450 moratoriums already in place nationwide.
items.title: Could a Data Center's Waste Heat Warm a North Carolina Town?

items.summary:
A year after its launch, the New England Heat Pump Accelerator is described as thriving, with more than 25,000 homes across the region expected to keep warm this winter using new energy-efficient, low-emission systems partly funded by federal money. The program — a joint effort among Connecticut, Maine, Massachusetts, New Hampshire, and Rhode Island — aims ultimately for 580,000 heat pumps installed in four years; though current progress is well short of that goal, early growth has supporters feeling confident about its chances.

The accelerator is backed by $450 million from the federal Climate Pollution Reduction Grants program created by the 2022 Inflation Reduction Act. It was cited as a rare example of a major Biden-era initiative making headway despite Trump administration efforts to cut clean energy and environmental funding.
items.title: One Year of New England's Heat Pump Accelerator Program

items.summary: An inquest led by Deputy State Coroner Joan Baptie is examining the neonatal deaths of four babies—two born by freebirth and one by homebirth in northern New South Wales, with a fourth also from that region—who died between 2022 and 2024. The inquiry will run for two weeks, during which evidence about advice and treatment given to the mothers before, during and after their births is expected to be heard.
items.title: NSW inquest examines deaths of four babies born by freebirth or homebirth

items.summary: China's foreign ministry announced on Monday that President Xi Jinping would hold his first trilateral summit with US President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen this week. The meeting is expected to take place on Thursday on the sidelines of an Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) leaders' summit in the southern Chinese city, where the three heads of state will engage in 'in-depth exchanges on safeguarding world peace and promoting strategic stability in major-power relations.' Foreign ministry spokeswoman Mao Ning described the talks as being 'of ground-breaking significance,' hours after Beijing confirmed their holding.
items.title: Xi, Trump and Putin to Discuss 'World Peace' at Shenzhen Summit, China Says

items.summary:
Gas has begun flowing from the Jackdaw gas field in the North Sea after UK ministers approved production last month, ending years of uncertainty and a court challenge. The energy secretary, Miatta Fahnbulleh, said the homegrown gas would help heat millions of British homes and businesses this winter while boosting energy security and reducing reliance on higher-emission imported gas. Jackdaw lies 150 miles east of Aberdeen and is operated by Adura under a joint venture between Shell and Norwegian state firm Equinor. Over its expected 11-year lifespan, the government says production will protect hundreds of jobs and add £2. 9bn to the economy.

Adura reports Jackdaw will provide about 6% of UK gas production, enough to power 1. 4 million homes, or roughly 2% of total UK demand once imports are included. Prime Minister Andy Burnham previously said the decision would increase domestic gas production by about 6% and support supply for more than a decade.
items.title: Jackdaw Gas Field Begins Production After Government Approval Amid Climate Debate

items.summary:
The trial of opposition politician and former presidential candidate Venancio Mondlane is set to shape Mozambique's political future and test citizens' trust in state institutions. From November 17, the country will watch as he faces five counts—including publicly advocating crimes and inciting collective disobedience and terrorism—following the October 2024 elections. If convicted, Mondlane could face more than 20 years in jail.

Mondlane denies all charges, arguing his public statements were meant to prevent violence rather than promote it. He claims he has sufficient evidence that his remarks went in exactly the opposite direction of what prosecutors allege. The post-election protests had two main goals: pressuring authorities to investigate extrajudicial killings linked to Mondlane's movement and finding out the truth about election results.

In those October 2024 presidential and parliamentary elections, Mondlane ran with support from the left-wing opposition party Podemos. Afterward, he refused to recognize official results, which saw Daniel Chapo of Frelimo declared winner.
items.title: Mozambique's Justice Under Scrutiny as Venancio Mondlane Faces Trial

items.summary: Miguel Ángel Félix Gallardo, the founder of the Guadalajara Cartel and widely known as “the boss of bosses,” died on Sunday at age 80. He had been imprisoned since 1989, serving two sentences totaling 76 years for organized crime and for the murder of DEA agent Enrique “Kiki” Camarena. His death followed a transfer from Puente Grande prison in Jalisco to the private Country 2000 Hospital just miles from where he was arrested 37 years earlier; his condition had worsened after house arrest was granted but never carried out due to objections over an electronic monitoring device.
items.title: Drug kingpin Miguel Ángel Félix Gallardo dies at 80 in Mexico City hospital

items.summary: Gordon Kidd, who runs Shifnal Cycles in Shifnal, says he is considering closing the business following a break-in last month that cost him about £20,000. Three customer bikes and a frame were stolen along with repairs to his shop. Alongside rising bills and what Kidd describes as a lack of government support, he warned the business may not be viable if financial pressures continue. West Mercia Police said it had received a report of a burglary on 31 October and that an investigation was ongoing.
items.title: Cycle shop owner considers closing after burglary and rising costs

items.summary: Singer Diljit Dosanjh performed his concert in Indore despite alleged attempts to prevent him from doing so, invoking poet Rahat Indori's famous couplet 'Kisi ke baap ka Hindustan thodi hai [India does not belong to anyone's father]' during the event. The Hindu quoted the singer as having stated that although several attempts were made to stop him from coming, he still came and never backs out once he commits to a performance. Dosanjh has faced restrictions on his concerts due to complaints that his lyrics allegedly promote alcohol, drugs, and violence, and he has also been criticized by Hindutva groups for the same reasons.
items.title: Diljit Dosanjh's Indore Concert Amidst Alleged Restrictions and Security Concerns

items.summary: Four IIT Delhi graduates developed the Aroleap X, a wall-mounted home gym that generates resistance through motor-driven mechanics rather than bulky weights. The founders — Anurag Dani and Rohit Patel, who shared an interest in fitness and robotics — began with their own problem: maintaining strength training without long trips to the gym or occupying space with racks, dumbbells and iron plates. They put roughly ₹25 lakh of personal savings into research and development, incorporated Aroleap Fitness Private Limited in 2020, built nearly 15 physical prototypes, and refined their manufacturing setup in Bengaluru before launching Aroleap X commercially.
items.title: Anand Mahindra says ‘bravo’: IIT Delhi graduates develop innovative home gym without weights; here’s how Aroleap X works

items.summary: A new analysis by Trase, a research initiative that maps commodity supply chains, attributes two-thirds of Indonesia's palm oil-related deforestation exposure to domestic consumption. In 2024, more than half of total production went into the Indonesian domestic market—an all-time high driven partly by biodiesel demand—and because this market does not impose strict sustainability requirements, much palm oil grown on deforested land is consumed within the country. For every 1,000 metric tons of crude palm oil (CPO) consumed locally, about 25 hectares was deforested; domestic consumption in 2024 corresponded to roughly 629,000 hectares—nine times greater than the exposure linked to exports to India, the largest foreign buyer. These figures reflect a ten-year historical attribution period rather than forest loss in 2024 alone.
items.title: Indonesia's Domestic Palm Oil Market Carries the Largest Deforestation Footprint

The Election Commission of India has assured the Supreme Court that voters who submit Form 6 to be reinstated after being deleted during the special intensive revision of electoral rolls will not face prosecution for doing so, per Bar and Bench. This assurance was conveyed through a supplementary affidavit filed on Saturday in response to a petition concerning Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, which alleged that decisions about voter roll revisions were taken without concurrence from the other two election commissioners. The Commission clarified that Form 6 submission does not constitute a false declaration under the Representation of the People Act as long as voters are not already enrolled elsewhere.

This clarification aligns with an October 14 Delhi High Court ruling, which held that apprehensions about false declarations were "misplaced" given Election Commission direction. The November 3 letter had noted voter hesitation because Form 6 requires applicants to declare first-time inclusion in electoral rolls.
items.title: Deleted voters will not be prosecuted for filling Form 6 for re-enrolment: EC tells Supreme Court

items.summary: On Monday, the Ministry of Defence (through its Directorate General of Defence Estates) and the Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment signed a Memorandum of Understanding in New Delhi to strengthen welfare for senior citizens living in cantonments under the Atal Vayo Abhyuday Yojana (AVYAY). The MoU was inked before Defence Minister Rajnath Singh and Union Minister for Social Justice and Empowerment Virendra Kumar. Under the arrangement, the social justice ministry will provide financial assistance toward operating and maintaining existing day care centres and senior citizen homes run by cantonment boards from their own budgets, while also funding skill training for geriatric caregivers. The Defence Estates Department has identified eight cantonments—Barrackpore, Belgaum, Jhansi, Khadki (Pune), Secunderabad, St. Thomas Mount and Delhi—for new day care centres; existing facilities in five cantonments will be strengthened, and senior citizen homes in Ayodhya and Lucknow will be augmented as funds permit.

items.summary:
International remittances help households meet daily needs and insure against hardship, yet the average fee for an ordinary transfer still stands at around 6%, far above the UN Sustainable Development Goals target of below 3% by 2030. New research by Flori and Limodio (2026) argues that a missing piece in explaining these high costs is the exchange rate risk borne by money transfer operators, or MTOs.

The exposure arises because an intermediary quotes an exchange rate and commits to delivering a fixed amount of foreign currency, but must later buy it at whatever price prevails. If the recipient's currency strengthens before settlement, the operator loses; in thin, underdeveloped FX markets—where depth rises steeply with GDP per capita—this risk cannot be hedged cheaply and so enters the marginal cost of every transfer. Competition alone therefore cannot remove it: competition squeezes markups but a corridor can still be highly competitive and very expensive.

Using the World Bank's Remittance Prices Worldwide database on 34,680 transfers across 339 corridors between 2011 and 2024, they find that fees rise with currency volatility rather than GDP. During episodes of exceptional instability, costs rose by about $1 on a US$200 transfer; in the quarter of the Swiss National Bank's unexpected abandonment of the franc's floor against the euro on 15 January 2015, prices jumped almost $1.60 relative to unexposed corridors—about 11% of the average cost ($14). The effect was stronger for thinner currency markets and less geographically diversified operators.

Estimating a model of the remittance market against a counterfactual with fixed exchange rates, they conclude that currency risk contributes about as much to fees as markups on average. Its share is highest in South America (24%) and sub-Saharan Africa (22%). The authors note this hits migrants twice—through higher prices now and reduced competition over time—and argue policy should promote deeper FX markets, affordable hedging instruments, and liquidity during market stress.

The study's boundaries include its reliance on the 2015 Swiss franc shock as a causal instrument for an event unrelated to migrant behaviour, and regional shares reported only as averages. Sources draw on BIS Triennial Survey data, World Bank indicators, Bloomberg, and Flori and Limodio (2026).
items.title: Currency Risk Drives Remittance Fees as Much as Markups Do

This post compares subjective beliefs about future job-finding and job-loss prospects from the New York Fed's Survey of Consumer Expectations (SCE) with their realized counterparts in the Current Population Survey (CPS). Before COVID, aggregate expectations aligned closely with actual rates: averaged over 2014 through 2019, the SCE expected a three-month job-finding rate of 55. 5 percent versus a CPS true rate of 57. 2 percent. The steep drop in realized three-month-ahead job finding at the end of 2019 reflected the unanticipated arrival of COVID-19; expectations fell only at its onset in March 2020, and although actual rates largely recovered to pre-COVID levels by 2021, expectations remained subdued. In the years after 2020, realized job-finding rates averaged 58. 8 percent from 2022 onward while predicted probabilities fell to 53. 0 percent, indicating persistent post-pandemic pessimism about finding a job.

This divergence was driven primarily by younger individuals and those without college education.
items.title: Can Workers Predict Job Finding and Job Loss?

Seniors' sexual needs are not merely private matters. They intersect with medical health, marital dynamics and social safety.

items.summary: Young adults in advanced economies have grown more pessimistic about their economic prospects in recent years, while gambling-like financial activities have proliferated. Costas Arkolakis, Spencer Y. Kwon, Dominic Russel, Claire Shi, and Hyunjoo Yang link these trends through a Friedman-Savage (1948) motive: when life goals such as homeownership or marriage seem out of reach, individuals turn to financial gambles. The authors test this theory using an original survey combined with millions of linked records from Korea's leading credit bureau, telecom provider, and credit card issuer.
items.title: Gambling for Goals -- by Costas Arkolakis, Spencer Y. Kwon, Dominic Russel, Claire Shi, Hyunjoo Yang

items.summary: In the NBER Working Paper 36011, Jitendra Aswani and Roberto Rigobon examine how sustainable investment affects corporate governance adoption. Using data on 3,944 sustainable bond issuances by public firms from 2013 to 2022, they apply a heteroskedasticity-based identification strategy that finds a 1% increase in sustainable debt (measured relative to total debt) raises the likelihood of adopting sustainable governance practices by 9. 2%. This adoption is associated with an improvement in environmental performance of 16%, according to structural estimates.

Under the rule from the Commerce Department, companies must obtain licenses to export, reexport or transfer AI chips and servers to data centers anywhere in the world if those facilities may provide compute to firms in China or other restricted countries.

The controls apply to entities based in a group of embargoed nations that includes China, Russia, Iran, North Korea and 18 others.
items.title: US Tightens AI Chip Export Controls to Block Remote Access for Chinese Firms

items.summary:
As Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) prepares to host its 33rd Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen, Guangdong Province from November 18-19, 2026, the gathering arrives amid heightened geopolitical tensions, rising global tariffs, and economic uncertainty. The meeting's theme—"Building an Asia-Pacific Community to Prosper Together"—underscores a central message: shared prosperity is best achieved through openness, dialogue, and cooperation rather than restriction.

The article frames China's approach as one of responsible engagement on the global stage, contrasting it with what it describes as reckless moves by other nations aimed at scoring domestic political points. A key illustration of this cooperative model is the China-Chile relationship. Chile, described as China's "oldest friend in South America," has enjoyed strong trade ties for over 50 years; nearly 40% of Chilean exports went to China and around 24% of its imports came from China in 2024—both higher shares than with any other trading partner.
items.title: APEC China 2026: A Pivotal Meeting for Cooperation

items.summary: At the Delhi launch of her memoir Belonging: A Journey of Love, Sonia Gandhi reflected on the moment she first felt a sense of belonging in India. She recalled that this feeling emerged when people in her husband Rajiv Gandhi's constituency accepted her after his assassination, and she described the 2004 Lok Sabha election victory as a significant milestone marking an important stage in her personal and political journey. Speaking about her relationship with former prime minister Indira Gandhi, Sonia said she was initially awed by and intimidated by her formidable personality but later learned discipline, punctuality, courage and determination from her.
items.title: 'I felt accepted': Sonia Gandhi revisits 2004 Congress win at memoir launch

items.summary: The article opens with a standard website notice informing readers that browsing implies agreement to the site's use of cookies under its revised Privacy Policy and Terms of Use, noting that cookie settings can be adjusted through the browser. It then pivots to an upcoming event: world leaders are set to gather in Shenzhen for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting.
items.title: Shenzhen in One Word: What Visitors Say

items.summary:
The Supreme Court ruled on Monday that pollution in the Yamuna has worsened despite substantial spending on cleaning the river, directing civic authorities and the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) to address the problem. A bench of Justices Manoj Misra and Manmohan ordered CPCB to monitor water quality at points where the river enters and exits states, Union territories, and districts—covering 520 drains that discharge wastewater into the Yamuna.

The court emphasized accountability: if water deteriorates on any parameter while passing through a jurisdiction, the concerned administration will be held responsible and penalized. However, the bench acknowledged practical challenges in improving sewage management.
items.title: Supreme Court Raps Admin Over Rising Yamuna Pollution Despite Heavy Spending

items.summary:
The Trump justice department warned Senator Elizabeth Warren of potential significant legal consequences if she fails to preserve records related to investigations into President Donald Trump, marking the latest warning sent by the DOJ to congressional Democrats about their plans to investigate the administration or its associates. In a letter from US attorney Aaron Reitz in Houston, Warren was described as eager to weaponize congressional investigations against Trump's private associates.

Meanwhile, air travel disruptions continued for a third day with more than 10,000 flights affected on Sunday following an extraordinary no-takeoff order blamed by the administration on faulty communications equipment. Transportation secretary Sean Duffy predicted a return to normal by Monday after more than 250 US-related flights were cancelled and there were delays to over 700 scheduled for Monday.

Trump shifted responsibility to the Biden administration, claiming old equipment needed replacement funding. Congress had passed a $12.5bn air traffic control package in 2025 as part of the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, with top House Democrats noting that $8bn remains unobligated and $11bn is unspent.

Trump also scolded a reporter for questioning his focus on White House renovation projects rather than FAA upgrades. Separately, Trump said he would not mind seeing Jensen Huang reinstated as Nvidia CEO amid an open letter with more than 165,000 signatories demanding his return after resigning over alleged extramarital affairs.

Trump is preparing to depart for Asia on Monday, beginning in Washington before traveling to Manila and Shenzhen. He will attend the Asean summit, meet Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin for their first trilateral summit, and participate in the Quad partnership meeting with India's Narendra Modi and Australia's Anthony Albanese.

In Alaska's US Senate race between Democrat Mary Peltola and Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan, 97% of ballots had been counted with Peltola at 49.9%, needing more than 50% to win as the state uses ranked-choice run-off elections.
items.title: Trump administration tensions with Democrats amid US air travel chaos and Asia trip

items.summary: Russia says it has recorded its largest Ukrainian drone attack since the war began, in which a landmark bridge linking Russia to occupied Crimea sustained minor damage and several oil refineries were hit. The Russian military intercepted and destroyed 2,049 drones over 24 hours, officials said, with around 600 flying toward Moscow alone, according to Mayor Sergey Sobyanin. Kyiv came under a record 17 air raid alerts in a single day. At least seven people were killed by Russian strikes, and attacks on energy infrastructure caused blackouts for 50,000 people.
items.title: Russia Reports Biggest Ukrainian Drone Attack of War as Crimea Bridge Sustains Minor Damage

items.summary: At the China (Hainan) Museum of the South China Sea, a wall of photographs pays tribute to generations of fishermen and captains. Among those honored are men who spent their lives navigating distant waters, passing on their knowledge and shaping the fishing culture of the South China Sea.
items.title: The Captains Who Shaped a Fishing Tradition

items.summary:
The annual UN climate summit in Antalya exposed a widening gap between ambitious climate promises and the money required to implement them, as negotiations entered their final week. Nearly 200 governments faced the recurring question of where funding would come from to turn pledges into action, with adaptation—preparing for already underway climate impacts—identified as the most visible shortage.

The scale of need is stark: a 2026 Adaptation Gap Report by UNEP estimates developing countries will require about $305 billion annually by 2035. Yet international public finance from developed to developing countries reached only $28. 2 billion to $31. 7 billion in 2024, an increase of just $1 billion over the prior year. Even if a commitment made last year to triple international public adaptation finance by 2035 is fully met, it would cover only 20% to 29% of estimated needs.

The wider climate finance dispute remains even more contentious.

The terms of financing matter as well.
items.title: Türkiye Climate Summit's Finance Gap Threatens Its Promise of Action

Japan is represented by two acts: metal-meets-idol trio Babymetal and prolific anime singer Lisa (LiSA). items.summary: Arion Kurtaj, a 21-year-old hacker from Oxford, pleaded guilty at Woolwich Crown Court to breaching Rockstar Games and several other companies. He had originally been deemed unfit for trial due to the severity of his autism and was sentenced to an indefinite stay in a secure hospital; however, doctors later assessed him as fit to stand trial, leading to his release into a normal prison in January. Kurtaj carried out the hack on Rockstar Games in 2022 while he was on bail for other hacking offences and under police protection, being housed in a Travelodge in Bicester to shield him from rival hackers who threatened him over stolen Bitcoin stashes. Using an Amazon Fire Stick plugged into his hotel room television along with a Bluetooth keyboard and mouse, Kurtaj stole internal company data including 90 clips showing nearly 60 minutes of gameplay from the unfinished Grand Theft Auto 6.

A new 2025 census counts just 382 North Atlantic right whales (Eubalaena glacialis), a decline of about 1. 8% from the 389 animals recorded in 2024, according to scientists at the New England Aquarium's Anderson Cabot Center for Ocean Life and NOAA. The population remains critically endangered by IUCN standards, with only around 73 females of reproductive age holding steady despite the overall drop.
